observations.title: OpenMacros: product scope and provider strategy
observations.content:
**What**: Feasibility + competitive analysis settled for OpenMacros (Expo 57.0.13 / RN 0.86.2 blank template). Decisions: (1) barcode uses OpenFoodFacts directly, NO AI; (2) body composition uses US Navy tape formula as the hard number, AI photo estimate is optional, shown as a RANGE, and excluded from the trend chart; (3) app must be fully usable with zero AI configured — AI is an optional accelerator; (4) provider layer = one OpenAI-compatible client (Gemini/Grok/DeepSeek/Groq/Ollama) + one Anthropic client.

**Why**: User wants a free alternative to paid trackers via BYOK. Research showed all competitors cost US$60-100/yr and MyFitnessPal paywalled barcode scanning in late 2022.

**Where**: /Users/felipesaracho/proyectos/openmacros (blank Expo template, only App.tsx/index.ts so far). Blueprint artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a008ab24-4b7f-4cb8-ab52-951963264f52

**Learned**:
- Anthropic EXPLICITLY PROHIBITS third-party use of Claude Pro/Max subscriptions; OpenCode removed that plugin in v1.3.0. Claude = API key only. ChatGPT Plus / Copilot / GitLab Duo allow subscription use but ONLY scoped to developer tooling, so they do not apply to a nutrition app. Copilot ToS explicitly forbids use as a generic model provider.
- "Sign in with ChatGPT" for third parties grants identity + API credits ($5 Plus / $50 Pro at launch), NOT subscription inference.
- Gemini has an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/) with vision + structured JSON; compatibility layer is beta and SILENTLY IGNORES unsupported params.
- expo-camera in SDK 57 scans ean13/upc_a/upc_e natively via onBarcodeScanned — no extra library.
- Measured OpenFoodFacts coverage Aug 2026: global 4,683,962 / Argentina only 15,769 (7,643 nutrition-complete) / Uruguay 1,961. Sampled 20 AR products: 18 had kcal+protein. Thin coverage is WHY label-OCR via AI matters.
- Published accuracy data on photo→calorie apps: ~33% underestimation, Cal AI -345 kcal avg, 26.9% MAPE over 16 nutrients, macros error 48-66%. Cal AI's advertised 92-97% is measured on single simple foods only.
- Existing open-source competition: OpenNutriTracker and Waistline already do free local tracking with OpenFoodFacts — differentiator must be the BYOK AI layer + body comp + portable format.
- MacroFactor's adaptive TDEE is the only retention feature in the category; data model should not preclude adding it later.

observations.title: Kraut-type-a-fuck display font: license risk accepted
observations.content:
**What**: The `Kraut-type-a-fuck` typeface (Mr.Fisk, 2003, blackletter) is adopted as the DISPLAY-ONLY font for the flesh ecommerce. It must never be used for body copy.

**Why**: The user explicitly chose it after being shown two verified problems, and accepted ownership of the risk:
1. LICENSE: DaFont lists it as "Free for personal use" — commercial use is not permitted. This is a commercial ecommerce. The user accepted this legal exposure as their own decision.
2. GLYPH COVERAGE: The font ships 98 glyphs total. A complete Latin set with Spanish diacritics (á é í ó ú ñ) and inverted punctuation (¿ ¡) needs substantially more. Spanish accented characters are almost certainly absent.

**Where**: Not yet implemented. Will land in the typography layer of the design system (globals.css / @font-face declaration) and in the pen.dev design canvas token set.

**Learned**:
- Mitigation agreed: declare the face via `@font-face` with a `unicode-range` restricted to the glyphs Kraut actually provides, so any missing character (ñ, á, ¿) falls through to the fallback family automatically instead of rendering tofu. No manual copy workarounds, no conditional logic.
- The actual supported glyph range MUST be measured from the real font file before writing the `unicode-range` — do not guess it.
- A commercially licensed blackletter with full Latin coverage was offered and declined. If the licensing risk is ever revisited, that swap is a single token change if the font is wired as a design-system token rather than hardcoded.
- Verified source: https://www.dafont.com/kraut-type-a-fuck.font

observations.title: g59records visual language reference (from screenshots)
observations.content:
**What**: Extracted the visual language of g59records.com from two user-supplied screenshots (loading screen + home). The site itself returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so these screenshots are the ONLY verified source. Do not attempt to fetch the site.

**Why**: The user named g59records.com as the visual reference for the `flesh` storefront. Deriving the design system from memory was explicitly rejected; this record is the evidence base for the design phase.

**Where**: Feeds the pen.dev design canvas and the shadcn token set. No code yet.

**Observed elements (from the screenshots, not inferred):**

1. IMAGERY — 1-bit threshold treatment. Every photograph is reduced to pure black and white with no midtones, heavy visible grain, xerox/photocopy character. Subjects are cut out and layered as collage, and they deliberately OVERFLOW their containing panel. This is the single most defining move of the aesthetic.

2. TYPOGRAPHY — blackletter throughout: nav items, the oversized headline, the subtitle, and even the footer copyright line. The headline has rough, dripping, distressed edges. A secondary scribble/marker script is used for the tiny "new!" tag. Note: the site carries almost NO body copy, which is why all-blackletter works there.

3. COLOR — the ground is pure black. Content panels are mid-grey (roughly #8a8a8a) with a scratched grunge texture. Type is white. Accents are extremely sparse: a yellow nav item ("Tour"), a red scribble ("new!"), and cream for "loading...". The ONLY saturated color on the page is the vertical rail of social icons at far left, which keep their native brand colors (YouTube red, Instagram gradient, Spotify green, SoundCloud orange).

4. TEXTURE — a distressed/scratched overlay of white marks sits on the black ground across the whole page, not just inside panels.

5. DECORATIVE FURNITURE — non-content ornament carries a lot of the identity: barbed wire strung horizontally across the full width (crossing over and under content), a horizontal filmstrip / contact-sheet strip of small thumbnails on a white band, a circular medallion above the nav, and a blackletter monogram mark in the corner.

6. COMPOSITION — heavy negative space, centered focal point, one dominant element per screen. The loading screen is a single skull on black. Nothing sits in a tidy grid.

**Learned / tensions to resolve:**
- CONFLICTING REFERENCES: g59 is a chaotic layered collage; the rotten-future product page the user also cited is a clean, structured, modern two-column commerce layout. These are opposite philosophies. The workable synthesis is g59 as SKIN (texture, 1-bit imagery, blackletter display, ornament) over rotten-future as BONES (layout structure, selector controls, numbered accordions). This must be stated explicitly or the result becomes an unusable mess.
- BODY COPY PROBLEM: g59 can set everything in blackletter because it has nearly no running text. An ecommerce has product descriptions, size tables, and shipping policy. A second, legible text family is mandatory. This aligns with the already-made decision that Kraut is display-only — see [[flesh/decisions/display-font]].
- PALETTE vs BRIEF: the user specified primary RED and secondary WHITE, but g59's ground is black with red as a near-invisible accent. In shadcn token terms these are not in conflict — `--background` black, `--foreground` white, `--primary` red — but how DOMINANT red should be is an open product decision, not a technical one.
- The 1-bit image treatment is a production concern, not only CSS. Options to evaluate: baked-into-asset, CSS filter chain (grayscale + extreme contrast + grain overlay), or SVG filters.

observations.title: sdd/flesh-storefront/explore
observations.content:
## Exploration: 3-product ecommerce storefront (flesh)

### Current State
Fresh `create-next-app` scaffold, single commit ("Initial commit from Create Next App"). Stack: Next.js 16.3.3 App Router, React 19.2.8, TypeScript 5 strict, Tailwind CSS 4 (`@tailwindcss/postcss`), pnpm 10.18.0, `reactCompiler: true`, `cacheComponents` NOT enabled (so the removed route-segment exports like `revalidate`/`dynamic` are still valid; `'use cache'`/`cacheLife`/`cacheTag` model is opt-in, not mandatory, unless the user later enables `cacheComponents`).
Only files: `app/page.tsx` (default template), `app/layout.tsx` (Geist fonts), `app/globals.css` (`@import "tailwindcss"` + `@theme inline` mapping `--color-background`/`--color-foreground`), `app/favicon.ico`. No `src/` folder, no `components.json`, no test runner, no `.codegraph/` index (correctly not initialized — indexing is the user's decision, and this 4-file scaffold does not currently justify it; re-evaluate once `src/modules` exists).
Display font decision already made and out of scope for re-litigation: `Kraut-type-a-fuck`, display-only, licensing risk accepted, mitigated via `@font-face` + `unicode-range` scoped to the font's real glyph coverage (must be MEASURED from the binary before implementation, not guessed).

### Affected Areas (future, nothing exists yet)
- `app/layout.tsx`, `app/page.tsx`, `app/globals.css` — will be rewritten; `app/page.tsx` becomes a thin composition root importing from `src/modules/storefront`.
- `app/producto/[slug]/page.tsx` — new dynamic route for PDP, thin wrapper importing `src/modules/product-detail`.
- `components.json`, `lib/utils.ts` (or `src/lib/utils.ts`), `app/globals.css` (again) — created/modified by `shadcn init`.
- New `src/modules/{storefront,product-detail}/**` and `src/shared/{ui,lib,fonts}/**` — domain code per screaming-architecture proposal below.
- No test runner exists; Strict TDD is active, so Vitest + RTL setup (`vitest.config.mts`, `__tests__/` or colocated `*.test.tsx`) is a prerequisite for any component work, with Playwright E2E reserved for async Server Components (Vitest cannot render them — verified in bundled Next docs).

### Approaches

#### 1. Catalog of exactly 3 products — layout strategy
1. **Single continuous editorial scroll (landing = catalog)** — one full-viewport section per product, oversized display type, no `/tienda` route; PDP reached via CTA per section.
   - Pros: turns scarcity into a brand statement; no empty-grid problem because there is no grid; matches the display-font decision (large type per section); one page to build.
   - Cons: less scannable than a grid; needs a wayfinding nav (jump-links) for return visitors; each section needs distinct visual treatment to avoid repetition.
   - Effort: Medium. **Survives mobile best** — vertical stacked full-height sections is native mobile UX.
2. **Separate marketing landing + `/tienda` catalog route, asymmetric 3-card composition** (e.g. one large hero card + two smaller cards, not a symmetric grid).
   - Pros: clean IA separation (marketing vs shopping), easier independent caching/testing, bookmarkable shop page.
   - Cons: still must solve "3 cards in an asymmetric layout" as deliberate design work (not just CSS); two routes/pages to build instead of one; risks the grid still reading as "small."
   - Effort: Medium. Mobile-safe only if each asymmetric composition is explicitly designed mobile-first (not just "the desktop layout shrinks").
3. **Standard grid, 3 products + 1 non-product brand/newsletter block filling the 4th cell.**
   - Pros: lowest implementation effort, most familiar pattern, reuses a plain CSS grid.
   - Cons: closest to the "looks broken and empty" failure mode the brief explicitly warns about; brand block competes with products for attention.
   - Effort: Low. Mobile-safest (trivial 1-column stack) but least novel.
   - **JUDGMENT (not verified)**: recommend Option 1, given the g59/streetwear editorial reference aesthetic, but this is a brand/product decision, not a technical one — flag to user.

#### 2. Product detail page (modeled on rotten-future.com, URL fetched and verified)
Verified via WebFetch of `https://rotten-future.com/producto/fire-campera-wash-black-1nb13`: two-column desktop layout; left = image gallery with carousel + "1/5" position indicator + 5-item thumbnail strip; right = title, dual price ("$X con transferencia" / "$Y en N cuotas sin interés"), color selector (with "— agotado" sold-out state per color), size selector (S/M/L), fit selector (SLIM / TRUE TO SIZE / BAGGY, radio-style); below = three numbered accordions `01 INFORMACIÓN`, `02 TABLA DE TALLES`, `03 CAMBIOS Y DESPACHOS`; bottom = "SHOP THE LOOK" (one curated companion item) + "TAMBIÉN TE PUEDE INTERESAR" related-products carousel (4 items on reference site).
Component mapping (screaming-architecture, `src/modules/product-detail/components/`): `Gallery` (MainImageViewer + ThumbnailStrip), `PriceBlock`, `ColorSelector`, `SizeSelector`, `FitSelector`, `InfoAccordion` (3 items), `ShopTheLook`, `RelatedProducts`. Shared primitives (Accordion, Carousel, Badge) come from shadcn/ui under `src/shared/ui/components`.
Mobile collapse: single column — gallery first (main image + position indicator; thumbnail strip likely becomes a horizontal scroll row or is dropped in favor of swipe, judgment call), then info panel stacked, accordions unchanged (already vertical), ShopTheLook + RelatedProducts as horizontal-scroll carousels (same component, narrower viewport).
**Caveat (explicit tool limitation)**: WebFetch converts to markdown and loses exact DOM classes/breakpoints, so precise mobile collapse behavior (does the thumbnail strip hide, become a strip, or turn into swipe-only?) is NOT verified from the fetch — it is my judgment based on common patterns. The user's forthcoming screenshots are the authoritative source and should be reviewed before `/design` work.
**Open product question**: reference site's related/shop-the-look sections assume a larger catalog; with only 3 total products, at most 2 "related" items exist. Needs a user decision: show only the 2 remaining products, hide the section, or repurpose as a single cross-sell card.

#### 3. Screaming architecture within App Router (verified against `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/02-project-structure.md`)
Verified Next 16 supports: route groups `(group)` (organizational, omitted from URL), private folders `_folder` (opts folder + subfolders out of routing — safe for colocated non-route code), colocation (any non-`page`/`route`/`layout`/etc. file inside `app/` is not publicly routable), and the `src/` folder as an official, supported top-level convention for separating app code from root config.
**Proposed structure**:
```
src/
  app/                     # thin routing shell — only composition
    layout.tsx
    page.tsx               # imports <LandingPage/> from modules/storefront
    producto/[slug]/page.tsx  # imports <ProductDetailPage/> from modules/product-detail
  modules/
    storefront/{components,lib,types.ts}     # landing/catalog domain
    product-detail/{components,lib,types.ts} # PDP domain
  shared/
    ui/components/          # shadcn-generated primitives
    lib/                     # cn(), price formatters
    fonts/                   # local font files + @font-face (Kraut-type-a-fuck unicode-range)
```
**Key adaptation vs the Vue/Vite article** (`dev.to/sergioazoc` screaming-architecture piece): its per-feature `routes/` folder cannot transfer literally because Next's router is filesystem-based and owns `app/`. The principle survives by inversion: `app/**/page.tsx` files become the thinnest possible composition root (import + render a page component from the matching `src/modules/<domain>`), so domain complexity — the part that actually needs to "scream" — lives entirely in `src/modules/<domain>`, while `app/` stays a low-complexity URL manifest.
**Alternative rejected (judgment)**: nesting modules inside `app/_modules/` via private folders. Rejected because it mixes routing and domain concerns in one physical tree and nothing enforces "app/ is routing-only" the way a separate `src/modules` root does.
Route groups: not needed yet at 2 routes (`/`, `/producto/[slug]`); defer until a second landing variant or distinct layout justifies `(marketing)`/`(shop)` groups.

#### 4. shadcn/ui initialization (Next 16 + Tailwind 4)
**Tool gap**: context7 MCP tool was requested by the task but is not present in this sub-agent's available toolset; used WebFetch/WebSearch against `ui.shadcn.com` as the explicitly-allowed fallback. Confidence is moderate on exact `components.json` defaults/CLI flags — should be spot-checked (context7 or `shadcn init --help`) before `sdd-apply` runs the real command.
**Verified via WebSearch**: shadcn/ui supports Next.js 16 App Router + Tailwind CSS v4 as of 2026 ("default SaaS stack" combo per multiple 2026 sources); Tailwind v4 is CSS-first (`@theme` directive replaces `tailwind.config.js`), OKLCH replaces HSL for color tokens.
**Command**: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest init` (pnpm confirmed as this repo's package manager), then `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add <component>` per primitive.
**Files touched (WebFetch-summarized, not verbatim-doc-verified)**: `components.json` created (style, `rsc: true`, `tsx: true`, `tailwind.css` pointing at `app/globals.css`, `tailwind.config` left blank for v4, `cssVariables: true`, aliases for `components`/`ui`/`lib`/`utils`/`hooks` under `@/*`); `app/globals.css` gets a `:root`/`.dark` CSS-variable block (`--primary`, `--secondary`, etc. in OKLCH) plus an `@theme inline { --color-primary: var(--primary); ... }` mapping block that exposes them as Tailwind utilities (`bg-primary`, `text-secondary`); `lib/utils.ts` created with `cn()` (clsx + tailwind-merge); `tsconfig.json` verified/updated for the `@/*` alias. `components/ui/*.tsx` files are created per-component by `shadcn add`, not by `init` itself.
**Setting primary RED / secondary WHITE**: not an init flag — edit the generated `:root` OKLCH values after init (or pick the closest base-color preset then hand-tune). This still counts as a "proper init" because the CLI generates the full token architecture (the `@theme` mapping block and the complete semantic token set — primary/secondary/accent/destructive/muted/border/ring, light+dark) — only the two hue values are edited afterward, categorically different from hand-authoring the whole CSS variable scaffold.

#### 5. Design-first constraint (pen.dev / `/design` canvas)
Verified via WebSearch that `/design` (aka "Claude Design" canvas) is a real, current (2026) feature: runs from a brief, produces multiple editable artboard variants as `.dc.html` artifacts, iterated visually, then converted to real code on request (sources: code.claude.com Week 34 2026 changelog, pen.dev, third-party write-ups).
**Ordering as a real tasks.md dependency**: design tasks (`design:landing-mobile`, `design:landing-desktop`, `design:pdp-mobile`, `design:pdp-desktop`) must block the matching `apply:*` implementation tasks. Because shadcn init (#4) produces the canonical token set, the true order is: shadcn init → tokens finalized (RED/WHITE applied) → `/design` canvas work → implementation. Designing before tokens exist risks the canvas inventing its own colors, forcing a manual reconciliation later — exactly the duplication the user wants to avoid.
**Token hand-off — two options, both with tradeoffs (open question)**:
  - Option A: feed the exact generated `:root`/`.dark` CSS block into the `/design` brief so artboards reference the same variables directly. **Unverified**: could not confirm from search results whether `.dc.html` artboards support importing/referencing external CSS custom properties.
  - Option B: treat the canvas as visual/layout reference only; implementation applies the already-finalized shadcn tokens, with a one-time manual visual-match check against the artboard. Safer given Option A's unverified capability, at the cost of a bounded manual step.
  - **Recommend Option B as default** pending a capability spike on Option A; this needs either a technical spike or the user's explicit tolerance decision.

### Recommendation
Sequence: (1) shadcn `init` + RED/WHITE token edit first (source of truth for colors), (2) `src/` + screaming-architecture module skeleton, (3) `/design` artboards for landing (mobile+desktop) and PDP (mobile+desktop) referencing the finalized tokens, (4) Vitest+RTL setup, (5) implementation per module, PDP-related-products behavior resolved with the user before building `RelatedProducts`. Landing/catalog layout (Option 1 vs 2 vs 3) is a brand decision to confirm with the user before design work starts, not something to default silently.

### Risks
- Font glyph coverage for `Kraut-type-a-fuck` must be measured from the binary before `unicode-range` is written (already known, carried forward).
- Rotten Future reference's exact mobile DOM/breakpoint behavior is NOT verified (WebFetch loses markup detail) — user's screenshots are the authoritative source, review before design phase.
- 3-product catalog breaks the reference site's related-products/shop-the-look assumptions (needs ≥2 unrelated products) — open product question.
- context7 MCP tool unavailable in this exploration session; shadcn/Tailwind findings are WebFetch/WebSearch-sourced with moderate confidence — re-verify exact CLI flags/components.json defaults before `sdd-apply`.
- pen.dev `.dc.html` artboards' ability to consume externally-defined CSS tokens vs. visual-only matching is unverified — real open technical question, needs a spike.
- No test runner installed; Strict TDD is active, so Vitest+RTL setup is a hard prerequisite before any component code, and async Server Components will need Playwright E2E instead (Vitest limitation, verified in bundled docs).
- No `.codegraph/` index exists yet; not a current blocker (4-file scaffold) but should be reconsidered once `src/modules` code lands.

### Ready for Proposal
Yes, with two explicit user decisions needed first: (1) landing/catalog layout strategy (Option 1/2/3), and (2) related-products/shop-the-look behavior at 3-product scale. `sdd-propose` can proceed and encode these as open decisions in the proposal if the user prefers to decide during that phase rather than now.

observations.title: FLESH brand identity from existing Tiendanube draft
observations.content:
**What**: The user supplied screenshots of the EXISTING FLESH storefront draft (built on Tiendanube) plus its hero banner asset. This is the real brand, not a mood reference, and it outranks the g59 reference wherever the two disagree.

**Why**: The user explicitly said to use this draft as the guide for COLOR HIERARCHY and for what the main banner image will be. Until now the only visual evidence was the g59 reference — see [[flesh/design/visual-reference-g59]].

**Where**: Design system tokens, the hero/banner component, and the pen.dev canvas. No code yet.

**Observed — wordmark and type:**
- Logo is "FLESH" set in a high-contrast SERIF, where the F is replaced by a RED cross/dagger glyph with a horizontal bar. The cross is the brand mark and is the only red element in the entire draft page.
- The banner asset reads "VOLUMEN I" in the same white high-contrast serif, with the numeral "I" in RED. Same device as the logo: serif in white, one red element carrying the identity.
- All UI text (nav "Inicio"/"Productos", section heading "Destacados", product titles, prices) is a LIGHT-WEIGHT, WIDELY LETTERSPACED SANS in white. This is a completely different voice from the serif wordmark.
- CRITICAL TENSION: the existing brand is SERIF, not blackletter. The user separately requested Kraut-type-a-fuck (blackletter) and cited g59 (blackletter throughout). Three display voices are now in play — serif wordmark, blackletter display, letterspaced sans UI. This must be reconciled deliberately, not accumulated by accident.

**Observed — color hierarchy (the user's stated guide):**
- Ground: pure black, including the header band.
- Text: white.
- Product cards: LIGHT GREY panels (~#d5d5d5) floating on black — note this converges with the mid-grey panels observed in the g59 reference.
- Badges ("20% OFF", "ENVÍO GRATIS", "35% OFF"): black pills with white text, anchored bottom-left of the card.
- Prices: struck-through original in grey, active price in white bold.
- Carousel arrows: solid black squares with white chevrons.
- RED appears in exactly ONE place: the logo cross. Nowhere else on the page.

**Observed — hero banner:**
- A three-panel horizontal strip of gym/bodybuilding footage: dark, desaturated, heavy grain, VHS/degraded-video character. Panels are hard-split with no gutter.
- Overlaid type: "VOLUMEN I" top-left, "YA DISPONIBLE" bottom-right in the letterspaced light sans.
- The imagery is NOT the 1-bit threshold treatment of g59. It is dark, low-key, desaturated colour footage that retains midtones. Do not assume the g59 image pipeline transfers.

**Observed — layout:**
- Header: search icon left, centered wordmark, account and cart icons right; nav ("Inicio", "Productos") on a second centered row.
- Full-bleed hero directly under the header.
- "Destacados" centered section heading, then a horizontal product carousel with side arrow buttons. The draft shows FOUR placeholder cards — with only three real products this carousel will look under-filled, which is the catalog problem restated in the user's own draft.

**Learned:**
- "VOLUMEN I" reframes the catalog problem. The three products are not a thin grid, they are a DROP — Volume I. That is an editorial framing, and it justifies a full-bleed, one-product-per-section treatment far better than any carousel or grid does.
- The user refined what they want from the rotten-future product page: specifically the lateral image carousel that scrolls through images with a FADE-IN per element, plus the right-hand column for browsing options. Not the whole page wholesale.
- OPEN CONTRADICTION for the user to resolve: they selected "red as a dominant/protagonist colour", but the draft they told me to follow for colour hierarchy uses red in exactly one place. These cannot both be true.

observations.title: g59 product page: color and type system decoded
observations.content:
**What**: Decoded the colour and typography system of the g59records product detail page from a user-supplied screenshot. This EXTENDS and partially CORRECTS [[flesh/design/visual-reference-g59]], which was based only on the loading screen and home page.

**Why**: The user asked how g59 uses its accent colour, then supplied the product page as evidence. This is the page type that matters most for the FLESH build.

**Where**: Design system tokens, product detail page components, pen.dev canvas. No code yet.

**THE CENTRAL FINDING — accent colour marks identity and navigation state, NOT the call to action.**
Yellow appears on exactly three things:
1. The product title ("lb runaway sweatshirt (camo)") — huge, lowercase blackletter, the single loudest element on the page.
2. The active item in the left category sidebar ("all").
3. The active top-level nav item ("Shop").
And critically: the ADD TO CART button is a plain dark-grey rectangle with white sans text. NO accent colour at all. The price ($85.00) is white, not yellow.
This inverts the standard ecommerce convention where the accent lands on the conversion button. Here colour answers "where am I and what am I looking at", never "click this". Because almost nothing is coloured, the product title reads as the loudest thing on screen without any size trick.

**TYPE SYSTEM — two families split cleanly by FUNCTION, not by hierarchy:**
- BLACKLETTER carries identity and content: top nav, the whole left category list, the product title, the price, the footer links (terms/privacy/refunds).
- UPPERCASE LETTERSPACED SANS carries functional UI and dense information: the "select size" label, the size buttons (S/M/L/XL/2XL/3XL), ADD TO CART, the spec list (SCREEN PRINTED LEFT SIDE RIB / EMBROIDERED HOOD / COMPOSITION: 100% COTTON / PLEASE ALLOW 4-6 WEEKS FOR DELIVERY), and the SIZE CHART button.
This is the direct resolution to the three-competing-voices problem flagged in [[flesh/design/brand-identity-current]]: display face for brand and content, plain sans for controls and specs. The FLESH draft already uses a letterspaced sans for UI, so the two systems converge.

**LAYOUT (product page):**
- Three columns on desktop: left category sidebar (right-aligned text), centre gallery, right info column.
- Gallery: product photo inside a WHITE box with dark grey bars top and bottom — a high-contrast island on the black ground. Magnifier icon top-right of the box. Chevron arrows («  ») sit OUTSIDE the white box, left and right. Position counter "1 / 3" centred at the bottom. Same counter device as the rotten-future reference.
- Right column order: title → price → "select size" label → size buttons row → quantity stepper (− 1 +) beside ADD TO CART → spec list → SIZE CHART button.
- Controls are all dark charcoal rectangles with white text. Flat, no radius to speak of, no borders.

**IMAGERY CORRECTION**: product photography here is NORMAL FULL-COLOUR product shot on white (visible camo texture, orange embroidered logo). It is NOT the 1-bit threshold treatment seen on the home page. The threshold look is reserved for editorial/artist imagery; product shots stay clean and literal. Do not apply a threshold pipeline to product photography.

**ORNAMENT**: barbed wire runs diagonally across the entire viewport, passing OVER and UNDER content including the header area — the ornament layer sits on top of the composition, not behind it. Heavy scratched grunge texture on the black ground. A skull medallion sits above the centre nav; a tiny skull glyph marks the active sidebar item.

**Learned / implication for FLESH**: mapping red to g59's yellow role produces a specific, non-obvious system — red on the product title and on active nav/category state, with a NEUTRAL add-to-cart button. That is a third distinct position, different both from "red as CTA accent" and from "red as dominant surface". It should be offered to the user as its own option rather than folded into either.

observations.title: FLESH color tokens: red is shadcn --primary
observations.content:
**What**: Red is the shadcn `--primary` token for the FLESH storefront. Full map: `--background` black / `--foreground` white; `--primary` red / `--primary-foreground` white; `--secondary` white / `--secondary-foreground` black; `--card` light grey (~#d5d5d5) / `--card-foreground` black; `--muted-foreground` grey for struck-through prices. OKLCH values exposed through `@theme inline`, generated by `shadcn init` and then tuned — never hand-authored.

**Why**: The user cut through a long design-philosophy discussion with a direct token-level answer: "if we put it in the shadcn design system it would be the primary". Verified against shadcn docs (context7, `/shadcn-ui/ui`, theming + customization) that `--primary`/`--primary-foreground` governs "Primary buttons and actions". So this decision settles a question that had been open separately: THE ADD-TO-CART BUTTON IS RED. That deliberately departs from the g59 reference, where the accent marks identity and navigation state while the buy button stays neutral grey — see [[flesh/design/g59-product-page-system]]. The departure is justified because the FLESH red cross wordmark already supplies the identity role g59 gets from yellow.

**Where**: Will land in `app/globals.css` (or `src/app/globals.css`) as the `:root` token block plus the `@theme inline` mapping, generated by `shadcn init`. Also must be mirrored into the pen.dev design canvas from the same source.

**Learned:**
- DESTRUCTIVE COLLISION, verified: shadcn's default `--destructive` is itself red (`oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)`). With a red `--primary`, "add to cart" and "remove from cart" become visually indistinguishable — a usability defect, not an aesthetic preference. Resolution proposed to the user and awaiting only silent acceptance: `--primary` keeps the brand red as a FILLED treatment, while destructive actions become RED OUTLINE on black. Same colour family, different hierarchy, unambiguous.
- SINGLE THEME: the site is black in every state. There is no light mode, so only one token set is needed. This roughly halves the theming work and removes the `.dark` block entirely.
- Verified Tailwind v4 / shadcn conventions: colours are OKLCH (lightness 0-1, chroma, hue 0-360), every colour follows the `name` / `name-foreground` pair convention where the base is the background and `-foreground` is text/icons on it, and `@theme inline` maps `--color-*` utilities to the raw variables.
- Related tension already resolved: the type system splits by FUNCTION not hierarchy — see [[flesh/design/g59-product-page-system]].

observations.title: sdd/flesh-storefront/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: FLESH storefront — Volumen I drop

## Intent

FLESH sells 3 products. The existing Tiendanube draft renders them in a 4-card "Destacados" carousel visibly under-filled with placeholders — the catalogue problem stated in the user's own work. But the hero reads **"VOLUMEN I — YA DISPONIBLE"**: these are not a thin catalogue, they are a *drop*. Reframing the site as an editorial volume release turns scarcity into the product story and removes the empty-grid failure mode by removing the grid.

Success: a black, type-led storefront where 3 products feel deliberate; a PDP with a fade-in lateral gallery and a right-hand option column; a generated token/type system; and a product data layer faithful enough to the real Tiendanube wire contract that going live is a source swap, not a component rewrite.

## Scope

### In scope
- shadcn init + single dark token set (red `--primary`), `@font-face` typography layer
- pen.dev artboards (`.dc.html`) for landing + PDP, **mobile and desktop**, before any app code
- Vitest + RTL harness (strict-TDD prerequisite); Playwright reserved for async Server Components
- `src/` screaming-architecture migration; `app/**/page.tsx` reduced to a URL manifest
- **`catalog` module**: Tiendanube-faithful mock data, wire types, anti-corruption mapper, money + locale helpers
- Landing: header/nav, full-bleed hero, one-product-per-section drop scroll, footer
- PDP `/producto/[slug]`: gallery (fade-in lateral carousel, framed image, external chevrons, `N / M` counter), generic option selectors, numbered accordions

### Out of scope
- **Backend, live API calls, cart, checkout, payments, orders** — removed entirely by the mock-data decision
- Search, accounts, CMS, i18n framework, analytics
- Volumen II content; light mode (there is none); 1-bit threshold pipeline for product shots

## Capabilities

### New
- `design-tokens`: single dark theme, OKLCH via `@theme inline`, generated by `shadcn init` then tuned
- `typography-system`: display/sans split **by function**, Kraut `unicode-range` fallback
- `product-catalog`: Tiendanube wire contract, fixtures, mapper, money/locale primitives
- `storefront-landing`: hero + drop sections + shell
- `product-detail`: gallery, generic option selectors, accordions

### Modified
- None (no existing specs)

## Approach

### Sequence (hard dependency chain, not a preference)

`shadcn init` → tokens finalised → **pen.dev artboards (mobile + desktop)** → Vitest harness → implementation.

Tokens come first because artboards drawn before them invent their own colours and force manual reconciliation later. Artboards block their matching implementation task: `design:landing-{mobile,desktop}` blocks `apply:landing`, `design:pdp-{mobile,desktop}` blocks `apply:pdp`.

**Scheduling note:** the `catalog` module is pure logic with no design dependency, so it can proceed in parallel with tokens and artboards. It is also the ideal strict-TDD slice — every unit is a pure function.

### Data source — DECIDED

**Mock data shaped to the real Tiendanube Product entity contract.** Not an invented convenience shape. The mock must be faithful *including its awkward parts*, so connecting the live API later is a source swap behind one boundary rather than a component rewrite.

Verified contract facts that drive real design decisions:

| Fact | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **Prices are strings**: `"price": "25.00"`, `promotional_price`, `cost`, `weight` | A money layer parses at the module boundary. **No arithmetic on raw API values anywhere in components.** Parse to integer minor units to avoid float error |
| **`attributes` and `values` are positionally correlated, not keyed**: product has `attributes: [{es:"Talle"}, {es:"Color"}]`, each variant has `values: [{es:"M"}, {es:"Negro"}]`; index *i* of a variant's `values` maps to index *i* of the product's `attributes`, with no linking key | The single most error-prone part of the contract, and exactly what drives the PDP selectors. The mapper derives option axes by walking attribute index positions across all variants |
| **Max 3 attributes**, up to 1000 variants | Selectors are built **generically over up to 3 attribute axes**, not hardcoded colour/size/fit. The rotten-future reference has exactly 3 selectors (colour, size, fit) — that matches the platform ceiling rather than being a coincidence |
| **`name`, `description`, `handle`, `attributes` are language-keyed objects** `{en, es, pt}`, never plain strings | Components must never read `product.name`. A locale accessor lives in the catalog module |
| **`description` contains HTML** | Needs a rendering/sanitisation decision (below) |
| `visibility` enum `visible \| unlisted \| hidden`, legacy `published` boolean retained | Filter on `visibility`; treat `published` as legacy only |
| `stock` number with sibling `stock_management` boolean | Sold-out state is `stock_management && stock <= 0`, not `stock <= 0` alone |
| `images[]` carry `id`, `src`, `position`, `product_id` | Gallery **must sort by `position`**, not array order |
| `categories[]` nested with `parent` / `subcategories` | Tree, not flat list |
| `tags` is one comma-separated **string** | Split at the boundary |
| Timestamps are ISO 8601 strings | Parse at the boundary |

### Where the types live — evaluated, not assumed

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **A. Types + fixtures in `src/shared/`** | Rejected. The Tiendanube contract is *domain* knowledge, not a generic primitive. `shared/` should hold `cn()`, UI primitives and fonts; putting the product contract there makes it a dumping ground and lets any component import raw wire types |
| **B. Dedicated `src/modules/catalog/` owning wire types, fixtures, mapper and helpers; other modules consume only a narrow mapped domain view** | **Recommended.** Screams "catalog", confines the live-API swap to one module, and makes the anti-corruption boundary structural rather than a convention |
| **C. Types colocated per consuming module** | Rejected. Duplicates the contract across `storefront` and `product-detail` and guarantees drift, defeating the single-swap-point rationale |

Option B, refined: the wire types are **not exported** from the module index, so `product.name` is unreachable from a component by construction.

```
src/modules/catalog/
  api/
    types.ts        # verbatim Tiendanube wire contract — internal, not re-exported
    fixtures/       # 3 mock products in true wire shape
    source.ts       # getProducts / getProductByHandle — the swap point
  domain/
    product.ts      # narrow view: Product, Variant, OptionAxis, Money
    map.ts          # wire -> domain, incl. the positional attribute walk
  lib/
    money.ts        # "25.00" -> minor units; formatting
    locale.ts       # pick({en,es,pt}, locale)
  index.ts          # exports domain view + source ONLY
```

### Design system (decided, do not re-open)

| Token | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `--background` | black | ground, all states |
| `--foreground` | white | text |
| `--primary` / `-foreground` | red / white | primary actions incl. add-to-cart |
| `--secondary` / `-foreground` | white / black | inverted surfaces |
| `--card` / `-foreground` | ~#d5d5d5 / black | product panels |
| `--muted-foreground` | grey | struck-through prices |

**Destructive collision (confirmable):** shadcn's default `--destructive` is red and would render "remove" identical to "add to cart". Resolution: `--primary` keeps red as the *filled* treatment; destructive becomes **red outline on black**. Hierarchy is carried by fill, not hue.

**Type split by function** (from g59's PDP, converging with the FLESH draft): display face carries identity and content (nav, category lists, product titles, prices, footer); light letterspaced uppercase sans carries controls and dense information (labels, size buttons, add-to-cart, specs, size chart, shipping). The serif wordmark is a **fixed logo asset**, not a type-system role.

**Imagery:** product photography stays normal full-colour on a clean background. Degraded/grainy treatment is editorial and hero only.

**Architecture:** screaming architecture by inversion — Next owns the filesystem router, so `src/app/**/page.tsx` is the thinnest composition root; domain code lives in `src/modules/<domain>/`, shared primitives in `src/shared/{ui,lib,fonts}`.

**Volumen II forward path:** drop sections render from a volume-grouped collection, so Volumen II appends a titled volume section rather than inflating one list, degrading into a volume index when volumes > 1 — designed now, built later.

## Affected areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `app/globals.css` | Modified | **Verified**: ships a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block today. Single-theme decision requires *removing* it, not retuning it |
| `app/{layout,page}.tsx` | Modified | move under `src/`, reduce to composition |
| `src/modules/catalog/**` | New | wire contract, fixtures, mapper, money/locale |
| `src/modules/{storefront,product-detail}/**` | New | domain code |
| `src/shared/{ui,lib,fonts}/**` | New | shadcn primitives, `cn()`, font files |
| `components.json`, `vitest.config.mts`, `package.json` | New/Modified | tooling |
| `next.config.ts` | Unchanged | **Verified**: only `reactCompiler: true`; `cacheComponents` stays off |

## Open decisions (need the user)

1. **Related products / shop-the-look at 3-product scale.** At most 2 candidates exist. Show the other 2, hide the section, or repurpose as a single cross-sell card.
2. **Destructive = red outline on black.** Confirm or reject.
3. **`description` HTML rendering.** Fixtures are authored, so the immediate XSS risk is nil — but merchant-authored descriptions arrive with the live API. Recommendation: sanitise from day one (or render a safe subset) so the swap cannot introduce a hole later. Confirm.
4. **Add-to-cart affordance with no commerce layer.** The red primary button is a central visual element but nothing transactional exists. Inert/disabled, or a local-only client cart with no checkout? Recommendation: inert for this change, since a local cart implies a checkout path that is out of scope.
5. **pen.dev token handoff.** Whether `.dc.html` artboards consume the generated CSS custom properties (Option A) or are visual reference only with a manual match check (Option B). Unverified capability; B is the safe default.
6. **UI copy language / default locale.** The draft is Spanish. This is now concrete, not cosmetic: it selects the key read from every `{en, es, pt}` object *and* interacts with Kraut's missing á é í ó ú ñ ¿ ¡.

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **Positional attribute/value mismapping** — a variant whose `values` length or order diverges from `attributes` silently produces wrong selectors | **High** | Assert the length invariant in the mapper and fail loudly; unit-test with a 3-axis fixture; it is a pure function, so strict TDD covers it well |
| Float error from parsing price strings | Med | Integer minor units in the money layer; never `parseFloat` in a component |
| Fixtures drift from the real contract, so the "swap not rewrite" promise fails | Med | Fixtures typed by the verbatim wire types; any contract drift becomes a compile error |
| Kraut glyph coverage (98 glyphs) breaks Spanish copy | High | Measure `unicode-range` from the real binary; fallback family absorbs misses |
| Kraut licence is personal-use only on a commercial store | Med | Risk accepted by user; wired as a token so the swap is one change |
| Scope far exceeds the 400-line review budget | High | Chained PR slices below |
| Three display voices accumulate by accident | Med | Function-based split is the rule; wordmark is a fixed asset |
| Enabling `cacheComponents` later | Low | **Verified in bundled docs**: removes `revalidate`/`dynamic`/`dynamicParams`/`fetchCache` in favour of `'use cache'` + `cacheLife`/`cacheTag`, "is not a rename-only change", and "can surface build errors for uncached data outside of `<Suspense>`". Do not enable here. Also verified: `revalidateTag` now requires a `cacheLife` second argument |
| Vitest cannot render async Server Components | Med | **Verified verbatim in bundled docs**; Playwright E2E is the documented fallback. Mock data is synchronous, so this may not bite until the live swap |

## Size forecast and PR slices

Honest estimate: **~2400 authored lines plus tests** — roughly 6× the 400-line budget. `ask-on-risk` will trigger. Removing backend/commerce did not shrink this much, because the faithful wire contract, fixtures and mapper are now definite work rather than deferred work.

| # | Slice | Est. lines | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Vitest + RTL harness, `test`/`typecheck` scripts | ~150 | — |
| 2 | shadcn init, tokens, remove dark media query, fonts | ~300 | 1 |
| 3 | pen.dev artboards (4 files, non-app artifacts) | n/a | 2 |
| 4 | `catalog`: wire types, fixtures, mapper, money, locale + tests | ~400 | 1 (parallel with 2–3) |
| 5 | `src/` migration + shell (header, nav, footer) | ~350 | 2 |
| 6 | Landing hero + drop sections | ~400 | 3, 4, 5 |
| 7 | PDP gallery (fade-in lateral carousel) | ~350 | 3, 5 |
| 8 | PDP generic option selectors (≤3 axes) + accordions | ~450 | 3, 4, 7 |

Slices 1–2 gate everything. Slice 3 gates 6–8. Slice 4 is the natural strict-TDD opener and unblocks the option selectors.

## Rollback plan

The repo is at a single commit with no application code, so every slice is independently revertable.
- Slices 1–2: `git revert`; removing `components.json`, `vitest.config.mts` and restoring `app/globals.css` returns the scaffold to its initial state.
- Slice 4: `src/modules/catalog` is self-contained with no consumers until slice 6.
- Slice 5: the `src/` migration is a file move — reverting restores root `app/`.
- Slices 6–8: feature-local under `src/modules/*`; reverting leaves the shell intact since `app/**/page.tsx` only imports.
- Token rollback is a single CSS block; font rollback is one `@font-face` + token swap.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Landing and PDP match the approved artboards at mobile and desktop
- [ ] Three products read as a deliberate volume, with no under-filled carousel
- [ ] One token set; no light mode reachable in any state
- [ ] Add-to-cart is red-filled; destructive is visually distinct from it
- [ ] No component reads a raw wire value: no `product.name`, no arithmetic on price strings
- [ ] Option selectors are generic over up to 3 attribute axes and derive from positional correlation
- [ ] Gallery orders images by `position`
- [ ] Replacing `catalog/api/source.ts` with live API calls requires no component change
- [ ] No Kraut glyph renders as tofu in Spanish copy
- [ ] `pnpm test` passes; every component and mapper shipped test-first
- [ ] `app/**/page.tsx` files contain imports and composition only
- [ ] Adding Volumen II requires content, not layout rework

observations.title: FLESH design system: token map, single theme, destructive outline
observations.content:
**What**: The FLESH colour and type system is settled. Four bindings:

1. **Token map** (OKLCH, exposed via `@theme inline`, generated by `shadcn init` then tuned — NOT hand-authored):
   - `--background` black, `--foreground` white
   - `--primary` red / `--primary-foreground` white
   - `--secondary` white / `--secondary-foreground` black
   - `--card` light grey (~#d5d5d5) / `--card-foreground` black
   - `--muted-foreground` grey (struck-through prices)

2. **Red is `--primary`, so the add-to-cart button IS red.** shadcn's `--primary`/`--primary-foreground` governs "Primary buttons and actions". This RESOLVES the open contradiction recorded in [[flesh/design/brand-identity-current]] (user wanted red dominant; the Tiendanube draft used red in exactly one place) and it deliberately DIVERGES from [[flesh/design/g59-product-page-system]], where the accent marks identity and nav state while add-to-cart is neutral grey. The g59 pattern was considered and not chosen.

3. **Single theme.** The site is black in every state. No light mode. One token set only.

4. **Destructive collision resolution** (CONFIRMABLE — proposed, pending explicit user acceptance): shadcn's default `--destructive` is red (`oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)`), which would make "remove from cart" visually identical to "add to cart" once `--primary` is red. Resolution: `--primary` keeps brand red as the FILLED treatment; destructive actions become RED OUTLINE on black. Hierarchy is carried by fill weight, not by hue.

**Why**: Three display voices and two competing red semantics were accumulating by accident across the g59 reference, the existing Tiendanube draft, and the user's stated "red as protagonist" brief. Left unresolved, the build would have inherited the contradiction.

**Type system split by FUNCTION, not hierarchy** (taken from how the g59 PDP actually behaves, and converging with the existing FLESH draft):
- Display face (Kraut, see [[flesh/decisions/display-font]]) carries identity and content: nav, category lists, product titles, prices, footer links.
- Light letterspaced UPPERCASE SANS carries controls and dense information: field labels, size buttons, add-to-cart, spec lists, size chart, shipping copy.
- The serif wordmark is a FIXED LOGO ASSET, not a type-system role.

**Where**: `app/globals.css` (to be regenerated by `shadcn init`), `components.json`, `src/shared/fonts/`. No code written yet.

**Learned**:
- VERIFIED by direct read: `app/globals.css:15` currently ships a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block. The single-theme decision requires REMOVING that block, not retuning its values. Easy to miss because shadcn also emits a `.dark` class variant.
- VERIFICATION GAP NOW CLOSED. An earlier revision of this record flagged the shadcn facts as unverified. The orchestrator has since confirmed BOTH against the official shadcn docs via context7 (`/shadcn-ui/ui`, theming + customization pages): the `--destructive` light default is exactly `oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)`, and the customization table states `--primary` / `--primary-foreground` = "Primary buttons and actions". The destructive-outline resolution rests on confirmed facts, not inherited assumption. Still worth a glance at the real generated `globals.css` after `shadcn init` in case the CLI's base-colour preset differs.
- Also verified via the same docs: every colour follows the `name` / `name-foreground` pair convention (base = background, `-foreground` = text/icons on it); OKLCH values are lightness 0-1, chroma, hue 0-360; `@theme inline` maps `--color-*` Tailwind utilities onto the raw variables.
- Product photography stays normal full-colour on a clean background. The degraded/grainy/1-bit treatment belongs to editorial and hero imagery ONLY. Do not build a threshold pipeline for product shots.
- SUPERSEDES the narrower earlier record at topic `flesh/decisions/color-tokens`, which covered only the colour map. This record is the superset and is the one to read.

observations.title: Product data source: Tiendanube-faithful mock, no backend
observations.content:
**What**: The FLESH storefront uses MOCK product data shaped to the REAL Tiendanube Product entity contract. Not an invented convenience shape. This REMOVES backend, live API, cart, checkout and commerce integration from the `flesh-storefront` change entirely.

**Why**: When the live API is eventually connected it must be a data-source swap, not a component rewrite. That only holds if the mock is faithful to the wire format *including its awkward parts*. A convenience shape would hide exactly the details that break components later.

**Where**: `src/modules/catalog/` (proposed). Wire types + fixtures in `api/`, mapped domain view in `domain/`, money and locale helpers in `lib/`, with `index.ts` exporting the domain view and source ONLY so raw wire types are unreachable from components.

**Verified contract facts** (source: https://tiendanube.github.io/api-documentation/resources/product, verified by the coordinator):
1. PRICES ARE STRINGS: `"price": "25.00"`, `"promotional_price": "19.00"`, `"cost": "10.99"`, `"weight": "2.00"`. Requires a money parse/format layer at the module boundary. No arithmetic on raw API values in components. Parse to integer minor units to avoid float error.
2. `attributes` AND `values` ARE POSITIONALLY CORRELATED, NOT KEYED. Product carries `attributes: [{es:"Talle"}, {es:"Color"}]`; each variant carries `values: [{es:"M"}, {es:"Negro"}]`. Index *i* of a variant's `values` corresponds to index *i* of the product's `attributes`. There is NO key linking them. This is the most error-prone part of the contract and it is what drives the PDP option selectors.
3. A product is capped at 3 attributes, up to 1000 variants. The rotten-future reference PDP has exactly 3 selectors (colour, size, fit) — that matches the platform ceiling rather than being a coincidence. Build selectors generically over "up to 3 attribute axes"; do NOT hardcode colour/size/fit.
4. MULTI-LANGUAGE OBJECTS: `name`, `description`, `handle` and `attributes` are language-keyed objects (`{en, es, pt}`), never plain strings. Components must never read `product.name` directly; a locale accessor is required.
5. `description` CONTAINS HTML — needs a rendering/sanitisation decision.
6. Other shape details: `visibility` is `"visible" | "unlisted" | "hidden"` with a legacy `published` boolean kept for backward compatibility; `stock` is a number with a sibling `stock_management` boolean; `images[]` entries carry `id`, `src`, `position`, `product_id` and MUST be ordered by `position`; `categories[]` are nested objects with `parent` and `subcategories`; `tags` is a single comma-separated STRING, not an array; timestamps are ISO 8601 strings.

**Learned**:
- Type placement was evaluated, not assumed. Putting the contract in `src/shared/` was REJECTED: the Tiendanube contract is domain knowledge, not a generic primitive, and `shared/` would become a dumping ground while letting any component import raw wire types. Colocating per consuming module was also REJECTED (duplicates the contract, guarantees drift, defeats the single-swap-point rationale). A dedicated `catalog` module makes the anti-corruption boundary structural rather than a convention.
- Sold-out state is `stock_management && stock <= 0`, NOT `stock <= 0` alone — a product with stock management off is always purchasable.
- The mapper is a pure function and is the natural strict-TDD opener; it also has no design dependency, so it can run in parallel with token and artboard work.
- Highest-risk failure mode: a variant whose `values` length or order diverges from `attributes` silently produces wrong selectors. Assert the length invariant at map time and fail loudly.

observations.title: FLESH scope decisions: no related products, inert cart, Spanish UI
observations.content:
**What**: Three user decisions closing the proposal question round for the `flesh-storefront` change.

1. **NO related-products / shop-the-look section.** With a 3-product drop, "you might also like" has at most 2 candidates and the visitor has already seen both on the landing page. The section is cut entirely — component, design and code. Reintroduce it when Volumen II exists and there is genuinely something to discover.

2. **Add-to-cart button is INERT for this change.** The red primary button exists as a visual element because it is central to the design, but it performs no action. Rationale: a local cart implies a checkout path, and checkout implies the Tiendanube integration, which is explicitly out of scope. Keeping it inert keeps the slice honest rather than shipping a cart that leads nowhere.

3. **UI copy language is SPANISH.** This is not cosmetic — it selects which key is read from every `{en, es, pt}` multi-language object in the Tiendanube contract, so the locale accessor resolves to `es`. Consistent with the existing Tiendanube draft ("Inicio", "Productos", "Destacados") and with the target market.

**Why**: These three were separated out from the proposal's six open items because they change WHAT gets built, not how it looks. The other three (destructive outline treatment, HTML sanitisation, pen.dev token handoff) were resolved by the orchestrator as engineering defaults rather than product calls.

**Where**: Scope boundaries for spec, design and tasks. Removes the RelatedProducts and ShopTheLook components from the build entirely.

**Learned:**
- The Spanish decision interacts with the display font and the existing mitigation already covers it. Footer links in Spanish ("términos", "política") carry accents that Kraut's 98-glyph set almost certainly lacks. The `@font-face` + `unicode-range` approach from [[flesh/decisions/display-font]] makes those characters fall through to the fallback family automatically, so no manual copy workaround is needed. This is a concrete case where that decision pays off — verify it renders correctly once the real glyph range is measured.
- Cutting related products removes a whole component tree and shrinks the size forecast, which matters given the proposal estimated ~2400 lines against a 400-line review budget.
- Orchestrator-resolved defaults recorded alongside: sanitise `description` HTML from day one (security default, not a product call, so the eventual live-API swap cannot open a hole); pen.dev token handoff uses Option B (canvas as visual reference, implementation applies the finalized shadcn tokens, one-time manual visual match) with a spike to test whether Option A is possible; destructive stays red outline on black — see [[flesh/decisions/design-system-tokens]].

observations.content:
# Design: FLESH storefront — Volumen I drop

Legend: **[V]** = verified against files/bundled docs this session. **[J]** = judgment.

## Technical Approach

One async boundary, pushed as far up as it goes. `src/app/**/page.tsx` must be `async` because **[V]** `params: Promise<{slug:string}>` (`docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/page.md:13,46-48`). Everything below it is synchronous, so it is Vitest-testable. **[V]** Next's own Vitest guide (`docs/01-app/02-guides/testing/vitest.md:9`): "Vitest currently does not support them [async Server Components]. While you can still run unit tests for **synchronous Server and Client Components**, we recommend using E2E tests for `async` components." The screaming-architecture decision and the testability strategy are therefore the same decision: thin `page.tsx` is not style, it is the mechanism that keeps ~all code unit-testable.

Data flow:

    page.tsx (async, ~5 lines)          <- ONLY async code
      await params -> getProductBySlug  <- swap point, sanitises + maps
      |
      v  ProductView (plain, serializable)
    <ProductDetail>  sync server  <- Vitest-testable
      +-- <Description html={SafeHtml}>   server
      +-- <InfoAccordions>                server (<details>)
      +-- <ProductGallery images>         'use client' (index state, fade)
      +-- <PurchasePanel axes variants>   'use client' (Selection state)
             +-- OptionSelector x N  +  PriceBlock  +  inert CTA

## Architecture Decisions

### 1. Catalog type boundary

The proposal claims non-export from `index.ts` makes `product.name` unreachable **"by construction"**. **Partly false [J]**: TS still allows `import type {...} from '@/modules/catalog/api/types'`. Non-export is encapsulation by *convention*, enforced only by path discipline.

| Mechanism | Strength | Cost | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Index-only export | convention; deep import defeats it | none | Keep (necessary, insufficient) |
| ESLint `no-restricted-imports` banning `**/modules/catalog/api/**` outside catalog | mechanical, CI-enforced | ~10 lines flat config | **Adopt** — `pnpm lint` already exists **[V]** |
| Domain type has no wire shapes at all | structural: wrong value is a type error | none | **Adopt — the real defense** |
| Separate pkg w/ `exports` map | truly structural | workspace overhead | Rejected: disproportionate |

The load-bearing insight **[J]**: the invariant is not "don't import the type", it is "no component holds a language-keyed object or a price string". If `ProductView.title: string` and `price: Money`, a deep importer must *also* re-implement source+mapper to do damage. Encapsulation + lint are belt; the mapped shape is braces.

```ts
type Money = { amount: number; currency: string }        // amount = minor units
type SafeHtml = string & { readonly __safe: unique symbol }
type OptionAxis  = { index: 0|1|2; label: string; values: string[] }
type VariantView = { id: number; combination: string[]   // parallel to axes
                     price: Money; compareAt: Money|null; inStock: boolean }
type ProductView = { id: number; slug: string; title: string
                     descriptionHtml: SafeHtml
                     images: ImageView[]      // pre-sorted by position
                     axes: OptionAxis[]       // 0..3
                     variants: VariantView[]
                     defaultVariantId: number; inStock: boolean; tags: string[] }
```

No `{en,es,pt}`, no strings-as-money, no `position` sorting left to callers.

### 2. Selector derivation over positional attributes

Derivation: `axes[i] = { index: i, label: pick(attributes[i]), values: firstSeenUnique(variants.map(v => pick(v.values[i]))) }`.

`Selection = ReadonlyArray<string|null>`, indexed by axis. **[J]** Deliberately mirrors the wire's own positional model — inventing a synthetic key would add a mapping that can itself desync.

Three-state availability (the reference PDP shows "— agotado", so sold-out is *displayed*, not hidden):

```ts
deriveAxisStates(product, selection, axisIndex)
  : Array<{ value: string; state: 'available'|'soldOut'|'nonexistent' }>
```
A value is `nonexistent` if no variant matches `selection` on all *other* axes; `soldOut` if such a variant exists but none is in stock; else `available`. `resolveVariant(product, selection)` returns the exact-match variant, or `null` while any axis is null.

**Invariant, failing loudly**: in `map.ts`, before any UI exists — `attributes.length <= 3` and `∀v: v.values.length === attributes.length`. Violation throws `CatalogContractError` naming product id, expected/actual lengths.

| Failure policy | Tradeoff | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Throw in mapper | loudest; with live API one bad product 500s the page | **Adopt now** (fixtures are ours; silence is the actual risk) |
| Result type | callers must handle everywhere | Rejected: ceremony at this scale |
| Log + drop variant | silently wrong selectors — the exact failure being defended against | Rejected |

`getProducts` lets it propagate today; **the swap point is where a future tolerant policy (drop malformed product from listings) belongs** — documented seam, not built.

Edge cases **[J]**, easily missed: **zero attributes** (A=0) must still resolve — `axes=[]`, `selection=[]`, `resolveVariant` returns the single variant so price/stock work; and duplicate combinations across variants (first wins, assert-warn).

Cost: ≤3 axes × ≤1000 variants = linear scan per render, trivial. No index map — noted as scale escape hatch only.

### 3. Money — integer minor units. Confirmed, with a Next-specific argument the proposal missed

| Option | Tradeoff |
|---|---|
| **Integer minor units** | exact for all three needed ops; **serializable across the RSC server→client boundary** | **Adopt** |
| decimal.js / dinero.js | correct, but instances are **not JSON-serializable**, so they cannot be passed as props into `PurchasePanel` — would have to be unwrapped at the boundary anyway | Rejected |
| Keep strings | pushes parsing into components — the thing being banned | Rejected |
| float | `19.99*100 = 1998.9999...` | Rejected |

Arithmetic actually required is only: display, discount % , min/max. All exact in integers.

**Parsing rule [J]**: never `parseFloat(s)*100`. Split on `.`, pad/truncate the fraction to the currency exponent. Exponent from a small table (ARS=2), defaulting 2 and asserting the currency is known — **[J]** minor units silently assume 2 decimals, and Tiendanube supports 0-decimal currencies (CLP/JPY).

**Formatting — hand-rolled pure function, not `Intl` [J].** `PriceBlock` is a client component (price depends on selection), so it renders on server *and* client; `Intl.NumberFormat` output can differ across Node/browser ICU versions (currency spacing), causing hydration mismatch. Single locale + single currency makes a deterministic ~10-line formatter (`$25.000,00`) that is a perfect TDD unit. Tradeoff: loses free multi-locale — not needed.

### 4. Rendering boundaries

| Component | Boundary | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `page.tsx` | async server | forced by `await params` **[V]** |
| `ProductDetail`, `Description`, drop sections, shell | **sync** server | keeps them Vitest-renderable |
| `ProductGallery` | client | index state, chevrons, fade |
| `PurchasePanel` (selectors + price + CTA) | client | price reacts to selection |
| `InfoAccordions` | server, native `<details>` | zero JS, accessible |

Rejected **[J]**: **URL state** (`?talle=M`) would make selection server-readable and shareable, but `searchParams` is a Promise **[V]**, making the page async — surrendering the testability the whole design is built on — plus router churn per click. Rejected on testability, not taste.

Rejected: shadcn/Radix `Accordion` for the numbered accordions — pulls a client boundary and a dep for pure disclosure. `<details>` is server-rendered. Tradeoff: styling the marker/animating height is fiddlier.

**[J]** `PurchasePanel` receives `{axes, variants}`, **not** the whole `ProductView` — otherwise `descriptionHtml` is serialized into the RSC payload a second time.

### 5. HTML sanitisation — at the mapper, behind a branded type

| Option | Tradeoff |
|---|---|
| Raw `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | free now (authored fixtures); opens XSS exactly at the swap the change exists to make safe | Rejected |
| **`sanitize-html` in `map.ts`, output typed `SafeHtml`** | allowlist, htmlparser2, no jsdom; one dep | **Adopt** |
| `isomorphic-dompurify` | battle-tested, drags jsdom onto the server | Rejected: weight |
| `html-react-parser` → React elements | avoids `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` entirely; most code + styling work | Runner-up |
| Strip to plain text | safest/simplest; destroys real merchant content (lists, bold) | Rejected |

**Structural, mirroring Decision 1**: the single call site of `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` accepts only `SafeHtml`, and `SafeHtml` is producible only by the sanitiser. Unsanitised HTML reaching the DOM becomes a *type error*. Allowlist: `p br strong em b i u ul ol li h2-h4 span a[href|title]`; force `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; drop non-`http(s)` schemes (kills `javascript:`).

### 6. Testing strategy

Vitest + RTL per Next's own guide **[V]** (`vitest.md:37,63-73`): `vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths`, `vitest.config.mts`, `environment:'jsdom'`. Add `test` and **`typecheck: tsc --noEmit`** — **[V]** neither exists in `package.json` today. Tests colocated (`*.test.ts(x)`), not a distant `__tests__/`.

| Layer | What | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| Unit (pure) | money parse/format/discount, locale `pick`, mapper + invariant throw, `resolveVariant`, `deriveAxisStates`, sanitiser allowlist | Vitest, node env |
| Component | sync server comps (ProductDetail, DropSection, PriceBlock) **and** client comps (Gallery, OptionSelector, PurchasePanel) | Vitest + RTL, jsdom |
| E2E | the 2 async `page.tsx` roots | **Deferred — see below** |

**Explicit tradeoff, as asked**: because async is confined to `page.tsx`, the Playwright surface is 2 files whose entire body is `await params` + render. **[J] Playwright is deferred out of this change**: installing and CI-wiring a browser runner for near-zero marginal coverage is a large slice. Accepted risk: broken `page.tsx` wiring is caught by `next build` + manual check, not automated test. Trigger to add it: the live-API swap making data loading non-trivial, or the first real navigation flow. Had `ProductDetail` been made async instead, nearly the whole tree would have fallen out of Vitest — that is the cost this boundary buys off.

Strict TDD: RED first everywhere. Slice 4b (mapper/selectors/money) is the ideal opener — all pure functions.

**[V] Gotcha**: do **not** put `import 'server-only'` on unit-tested modules. It is not installed (no `node_modules/server-only`), and **[V]** Next handles it internally ("The contents of these packages from NPM are not used by Next.js" — `05-server-and-client-components.md:602`), so under Vitest it would fail resolution. Restrict it to `source.ts`, or alias it in `vitest.config.mts`.

## Where types and fixtures live — proposal's reasoning re-checked

Both rejections **hold [J]**: `src/shared/` is importable by everyone (defeats Decision 1) and a vendor contract is domain knowledge, not a primitive; per-module colocation guarantees drift. But the proposal missed a fourth option:

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `src/infrastructure/tiendanube/` (hexagonal adapter layer) | The textbook answer, and right if a second vendor appears. **Rejected now**: splits the catalog domain across two trees, stops the tree screaming "catalog", adds isolation the module boundary already provides. **Promotion path recorded**: on a second vendor, `api/` lifts out; the mapper stays in catalog. |

**Fixtures as `.ts`, not `.json` [J]**: `resolveJsonModule` is on **[V]**, so JSON imports infer wide structural types and contract drift compiles clean — the proposal's "drift becomes a compile error" promise would silently fail. Use `export const products = [...] satisfies TiendanubeProduct[]` — `satisfies` both checks and preserves literal types.

## Kraut `@font-face` + `unicode-range`

**[V]** `next/font/local` accepts `declarations: [{prop, value}]`, "font face descriptor key-value pairs" (`font.md:234-244`), and `unicode-range` is a valid descriptor — so `{prop:'unicode-range', value:'U+0020-007E,...'}` works while keeping Next's self-hosting/preload. Preferred over a hand-written `@font-face`.

**Critical [J]**: the token must be a **stack**, not one family — `--font-display: "Kraut", "<fallback display>", sans-serif`. `unicode-range` makes the browser use Kraut only for in-range codepoints; out-of-range chars (á é í ó ú ñ ¿ ¡ — Spanish is now confirmed UI copy) fall to the *next family in the stack*. With a single family they land on an arbitrary default.

**Measurement belongs in the typography slice (2), as a blocking sub-task before the `@font-face` is written** — not a build step (the font is static; a build step is ceremony). Measure via `fontTools` (`TTFont(f)['cmap'].getBestCmap().keys()`) or `fc-query`; commit the range as a **literal** with the generating command in a comment so it is reproducible. **Never guessed.**

## globals.css — the removal is bigger than one block

**[V] Confirmed by direct read**: `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` at `app/globals.css:15-20`. But **[J]** deleting only that leaves `:root` holding *light* values (`#ffffff`/`#171717`, lines 4-5) and `body{font-family: Arial...}` (line 25) overriding the type system. Also, `shadcn init` **rewrites** this file emitting `:root` + `.dark`. Correct sequence: (1) let init generate, (2) collapse to one set by hoisting dark values into `:root`, (3) delete the `.dark` block, (4) drop the Arial rule, (5) assert no `prefers-color-scheme`/`dark` class/`next-themes` remains.

**[V]** `tsconfig.json` maps `@/*` → `./*`. The `src/` migration **requires** changing it to `./src/*` — unmentioned in the proposal, and it silently breaks every import if missed.

## Threat Matrix

The reference matrix covers shell/git/PR/executable-classification boundaries only. All rows **N/A**: this change adds no shell commands, subprocesses, git or PR automation, and no file-classification or process integration.

| Boundary | Applicability |
|---|---|
| Documentation-like paths | N/A — no file classification or execution |
| Git repository selection | N/A — no VCS automation |
| Commit state / Push state / PR commands | N/A — no VCS or PR automation |

Genuinely applicable web-input boundaries, carried to tasks: **(a)** `[slug]` is user-controlled — it may only key a lookup over the fixture set, never touch fs/path/network; unknown slug → `notFound()`, RED test for unknown + traversal-shaped slug. **(b)** HTML injection via `description` — Decision 5; RED tests for `<script>`, `onerror=`, and `javascript:` href.

## PR slices — decomposition re-checked

Proposal: 8 slices, ~2400 lines "plus tests". **[J]** Including tests the real count is ~2800-3000 → 7x the 400-line budget, so the estimate is credible but the slicing is not tight enough. Four problems:

1. **Slice 3 (artboards) is not a PR** — pen.dev `.dc.html` are non-app artifacts. Reclassify as a **gate/milestone**, not a reviewable code PR.
2. **Slice 4 (~400) is at budget and mixes kinds** — ~300 lines of inert fixture data would hide ~150 lines of the riskiest logic in one diff. Split.
3. **Slice 5 mixes a file move with new UI** — git rename detection degrades when content changes land alongside moves, making the diff unreviewable.
4. **Slice 8 (~450) is over budget** and accordions are independent of selectors.

Revised (each builds green and is independently revertable):

| # | Slice | Est. | Depends |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Vitest+RTL harness, `test`/`typecheck` scripts | ~150 | — |
| 2 | shadcn init, single-theme collapse, Arial removal, fonts + measured `unicode-range` | ~300 | 1 |
| G | **Artboard gate** (mobile+desktop, landing+PDP) | n/a | 2 |
| 4a | Wire types + `satisfies` fixtures (declarative, low risk) | ~380 | 1 |
| 4b | mapper + invariant + money + locale + selectors + tests (dense logic) | ~330 | 4a |
| 4c | sanitiser + `SafeHtml` + allowlist tests | ~120 | 4a |
| 5a | **Pure `src/` move + tsconfig `@/*` → `./src/*`**, zero content change | ~80 | 2 |
| 5b | Shell: header, nav, footer | ~280 | 5a, G |
| 6a | Landing hero | ~200 | 5b |
| 6b | Drop sections (volume-grouped) | ~250 | 6a, 4b |
| 7 | PDP gallery (client, fade carousel) | ~350 | 5b, G |
| 8a | PDP option selectors over ≤3 axes + PriceBlock + inert CTA | ~300 | 7, 4b |
| 8b | `<details>` accordions | ~150 | 7 |

11 code PRs + 1 gate. Feature Branch Chain: PR 1 targets the tracker branch, each later PR targets its immediate predecessor. 4a/4b/4c form a clean strict-TDD opening chain parallel to 2.

## Migration / Rollout

No data migration. Single commit, no app code — every slice is `git revert`-able. 5a is a pure move, so reverting restores root `app/`.

## Open Questions

- [ ] Currency exponent table: confirm ARS-only, or generalise if Tiendanube may return CLP/JPY.
- [ ] pen.dev Option A (artboards consuming generated CSS custom properties) still unverified; Option B (visual reference + manual match) remains the default.

Source of truth: design (`sdd/flesh-storefront/design`) wins over proposal where they conflict. 11 code PRs + 1 gate. Chain strategy: **decided — `feature-branch-chain`**. The chain as a whole remains `feature-branch-chain` across separate slices; this exception does not fold PR4a into any other slice or change the rest of the sequencing.
Chained PRs recommended: Yes

**PR4a `size:exception` — recorded, not an open flag.** PR4a stays ONE slice at ~560 lines, explicitly accepted by the user rather than split. Justification: PR4a's content is largely **declarative** — Zod schemas, `z.infer`-derived types, `satisfies` fixtures, and a `CatalogPort` interface. It reviews mechanically: does the schema match the verbatim wire contract, do the fixtures satisfy it, does the mock implement the port. The genuinely risky logic — the positional-correlation mapper, money parsing, locale accessor, selector derivation — lives entirely in **PR4b**, which remains its own small, isolated, behavior-dense slice (~330 lines). The line count in PR4a is concentrated in contract definition, not in behavior, which is why the exception is reasonable here specifically and is not a precedent for exempting other slices.

## Runtime Attempt Ledger — Lockfile Churn Note

**Recorded for future slices that install dependencies.** The native runtime
attempt ledger counts EVERY changed line, including generated lockfiles —
there is no exclusion flag for `pnpm-lock.yaml`/similar generated files;
`--max-changed-lines` is the only lever. PR1's first runtime-attempt
objective was blocked on this: `pnpm-lock.yaml` alone contributed 1088 of

runtime attempt's `--max-changed-lines` for lockfile churn up front, not
just for the authored diff — this is separate from, and in addition to, the

from the authored-risk count but still requires them in receipt validation.

### Suggested Work Units (Feature Branch Chain — base branches)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Vitest+RTL harness (incl. `server-only` alias) | tracker | `pnpm test` (smoke) | N/A | remove devDeps + `vitest.config.mts` |
| 4a | **`size:exception`.** Zod wire schemas + `z.infer` types + `CatalogPort` interface + `server-only`-marked mock source + fixtures | PR1 | `pnpm test catalog/api` | N/A — local fixtures only | delete `catalog/api/**` |
| 4b | mapper + invariant + money + locale + selectors | 4a | `pnpm test catalog/domain catalog/lib` | N/A | delete `catalog/domain`, `catalog/lib` |
| 4c | sanitiser + `SafeHtml` + allowlist | 4b | `pnpm test catalog/lib/sanitize` | N/A | remove `sanitize-html` + `sanitize.ts` |
| 2 | shadcn tokens, single theme, fonts + measured `unicode-range` | 4c | `pnpm test app/globals` | N/A | revert `globals.css`, drop `components.json` |
| G | Artboard gate (mobile+desktop, landing+PDP) | n/a — milestone | N/A — non-app artifact | manual visual match vs. finalized tokens | delete `.dc.html` files |
| 5a | Pure `src/` move + tsconfig `@/*`→`./src/*` | PR2 | `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` | N/A | `git revert` restores root `app/` |
| 5b | Shell: header, nav, footer (requires GATE approved) | 5a | `pnpm test shared/ui` | N/A | feature-local |
