observations.content:
# Cart Specification

Legend: [V] verified this session against a file. [J] orchestrator judgment, derived from the user's stated preference rather than an explicit answer — the user may overturn.

## Purpose

Cart domain, persistence/drift handling, the transfer-discount policy, and the `Finalizar compra` checkout seam. Full spec — no prior cart spec exists.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Cart line item lifecycle
The cart MUST add, merge, adjust, and remove lines without ever holding two lines for one variant.

#### Scenario: Add new variant
- GIVEN an empty cart, WHEN a variant not present is added, THEN a line is created at quantity 1.

#### Scenario: Merge instead of append
- GIVEN a line exists for variant V, WHEN V is added again, THEN its quantity increments; no second line appears.

#### Scenario: Decrement to zero removes the line
- GIVEN a line at quantity 1, WHEN decremented, THEN the line is removed.

#### Scenario: Explicit remove and clear
- GIVEN a non-empty cart, WHEN a line is removed or the cart cleared, THEN that line, or all lines, disappear immediately.

### Requirement: Totals in integer minor units, discount applied once
Subtotal, discount, and total MUST be computed in integer minor units, no floats [V] `lib/money.ts`. The transfer discount MUST apply once to the subtotal, never per line.

#### Scenario: Artboard arithmetic holds exactly
- GIVEN 3 lines at $27.000, WHEN totals compute, THEN subtotal $81.000, discount $8.100, total $72.900, zero rounding drift.

### Requirement: Transfer discount rate is injectable
The rate MUST NOT be a module constant read at call sites; it MUST come through a parameter or policy provider so the source can change without editing consumers.

#### Scenario: Rate source changes, consumers untouched
- GIVEN the rate is supplied by a policy provider, WHEN its value changes, THEN no PDP or cart call site is modified.

### Requirement: Transfer discount stacks on the effective price
The discount MUST apply to a line's current effective price (promotional if present, list otherwise), never the pre-promotion price.

#### Scenario: Promo plus transfer discount
- GIVEN a variant has an active promotional price, WHEN the transfer discount applies, THEN it computes on the promotional price.

### Requirement: One shared discount policy for PDP and cart
The PDP `PriceBlock` and the cart summary MUST call the same policy function.

#### Scenario: Identical discounted figure
- GIVEN one variant's effective price, WHEN PDP and cart each render its transfer price, THEN both amounts match exactly.

### Requirement: Cart persists across browser sessions
The cart MUST survive a reload or new session via durable client storage, no expiry.

#### Scenario: Reload preserves the cart
- GIVEN a cart with lines, WHEN the browser closes and reopens, THEN the same lines and quantities return.

### Requirement: Rehydration reconciles against the live catalog
Every persisted line MUST be checked against current catalog state (`inStock` [V] `domain/product.ts:34,50`, price) before being trusted. The cart is not a price lock: it must never present a total the real store would not honour.

#### Scenario: Variant no longer exists [J]
- GIVEN a persisted variant id absent from the catalog, WHEN the cart rehydrates, THEN the line is removed and the visitor is notified that an item was removed. The catalog can no longer supply that item's name or image, so the notice states a removal happened without naming it — an honest asymmetry with the out-of-stock case, not an oversight.

#### Scenario: Variant now out of stock
- GIVEN a persisted variant is now `inStock: false`, WHEN the cart rehydrates, THEN the line is removed automatically and the visitor is notified it was removed and why, naming it, since the catalog can still supply its identity. It is never kept flagged-but-present, and the CTA is never blocked on it — the cost of losing the item unseen is accepted.

#### Scenario: Variant price changed
- GIVEN a persisted line's stored price differs from the catalog's current price, WHEN the cart rehydrates, THEN the price updates to the current catalog price and the visitor sees a notice that it changed.

### Requirement: Drift notices persist until seen
Every rehydration-time drift outcome — a removal (missing or out-of-stock variant) or a price change — MUST remain visible to the visitor after the fact, not a transient message tied to the instant rehydration ran. The visitor MUST be able to see what changed and why the next time they open the cart, even if that leaves the cart empty. A notice MUST name the affected item when the catalog can still supply its identity, and MUST still inform the visitor when it cannot.

#### Scenario: Notice survives an emptied cart
- GIVEN rehydration removed the cart's only line, whether missing from the catalog or out of stock, WHEN the visitor later opens the cart, THEN they see the empty state together with a notice that an item was removed, named only if the catalog could still supply its identity.

#### Scenario: Price-change notice remains visible
- GIVEN rehydration adjusted a line's price, WHEN the visitor opens the cart, THEN the notice that the price changed is still visible, not shown only once at the moment of rehydration.

### Requirement: Checkout CTA state machine
`Finalizar compra` MUST call `CheckoutPort.startCheckout` and render exactly one of idle, pending, or unavailable; it MUST NOT hardcode a success branch.

#### Scenario: Idle, pending, unavailable
- GIVEN a valid cart, the CTA is idle until activated, shows pending until the port resolves, and renders `unavailable` honestly with no navigation when that is the outcome.

#### Scenario: Rejected is a checkout-time concern, not a rehydration-time one
- GIVEN a cart with no known drift after rehydration, WHEN `startCheckout` resolves with `status: "rejected"` (a live integration finding stock or price conflict at the moment of checkout), THEN the CTA renders that rejection with the affected lines. Rehydration drift and checkout-time rejection are separate moments; resolving one does not make the other outcome unreachable.

### Requirement: Checkout and empty-state copy is ASCII-only
Display-font Spanish copy MUST avoid accented characters [V] Kraut's `unicode-range` is ASCII-only per the approved design.

#### Scenario: No accents in display strings
- GIVEN copy rendered in `$font-display`, THEN it has no accented characters (e.g. "Finalizar compra", "Tu carrito esta vacio").

### Requirement: `cart/api/**` is encapsulated
A deep import of `@/modules/cart/api/*` from outside the module MUST fail `pnpm lint`, mirroring the catalog rule [V] `eslint.config.mjs:25-47`.

#### Scenario: Deep import fails lint
- GIVEN a file outside `src/modules/cart`, WHEN it imports `cart/api/**` directly, THEN `pnpm lint` errors.

### Requirement: Empty cart state
The cart MUST render a distinct empty state with zero lines: no discount summary, no CTA.

#### Scenario: Empty cart
- GIVEN zero lines, WHEN the cart opens, THEN the empty state shows instead of line items and totals.

observations.title: flesh-cart: comportamiento de deriva del catálogo al rehidratar el carrito
observations.content:
**What**: Decisiones del usuario sobre qué hace el carrito cuando el catálogo cambió entre que se persistió y se rehidrató (2026-08-31).

1. **Variante SIN STOCK → se elimina sola la línea y se avisa.** No se mantiene marcada, no se bloquea el CTA.
2. **Variante con PRECIO CAMBIADO → se adopta el precio actual del catálogo y se avisa.** No se sostiene el precio viejo.
3. (Ya definido en el proposal) **Variante que ya no existe → se descarta silenciosamente.**

**Why**:
- Sin stock: el usuario priorizó que el carrito quede siempre consistente por encima de que el visitante vea la línea muerta. Aceptó el costo declarado: el visitante pierde el ítem sin verlo primero.
- Precio: el carrito no es un congelamiento de precio. Sostener el precio viejo mostraría un total que la tienda real no va a cobrar, y el día de la integración Tiendanube lo rechazaría igual.

**Where**: `sdd/flesh-cart/spec` (requiere corrección, ver abajo) y `sdd/flesh-cart/design`.

**Learned**:
- **CORRIGE AL SPEC.** `sdd/flesh-cart/spec` había especificado para sin-stock: mantener la línea marcada como no disponible, excluirla del total y **bloquear el CTA hasta que se saque**. El agente lo marcó explícitamente como juicio propio `[J]` y no como requisito derivado, y el usuario lo revirtió. La decisión válida es eliminar y avisar.
- **La pregunta de "bloqueo duro vs aviso con override" queda sin objeto** para el caso sin-stock: si la línea se elimina, no queda nada que bloquear.
- **`CheckoutOutcome.rejected` NO queda sin uso.** La rehidratación y el checkout son dos momentos distintos: la deriva se resuelve al recuperar el carrito, pero la integración real de Tiendanube igual puede rechazar por stock o precio en el momento de cerrar. El branch sigue teniendo sentido para el futuro.
- **Consecuencia de diseño a resolver**: si la línea se elimina sola, el aviso tiene que sobrevivir lo suficiente para ser visto — incluido el caso de un carrito de un solo ítem, donde el visitante vuelve a un carrito vacío. El aviso no puede ser un mensaje efímero atado a que el drawer esté abierto en ese instante.

observations.title: sdd/flesh-cart/design
observations.content:
# Design: FLESH cart — domain, persistence, and the checkout seam

Legend: **[V]** verified against a file read this session (path cited). **[J]** judgment.
Refines `sdd/flesh-cart/proposal`. Where they differ, this document and `flesh/decisions/cart-question-round` win.

## The finding that reshapes the proposal

**[V]** `src/modules/catalog/api/source.ts:7` carries `import "server-only"`, and **[V]** `src/modules/catalog/index.ts:14` re-exports `getProducts`/`getProductByHandle` from it as **values**. **[V]** `05-server-and-client-components.md:580`: importing a `server-only` module into a Client Component is a **build-time error**.

Therefore the proposal's plan — "rehydration validates stored lines against `CatalogPort`" — **cannot run in the client provider**. The catalog is unreachable from client code.

Consequence, and the spine of this design: **the catalog is projected into the client as serializable data from the server layout**, and everything the cart does with it (reconciliation, availability checks) becomes a **pure, synchronous function over that projection**. That is not a workaround; it is what makes the whole reconciliation pipeline unit-testable with no jsdom, no fake timers, no await.

Second consequence: **cart client files must never import `@/modules/catalog` for a value** — `import type` only (erased at compile time). **[V]** `vitest.config.mts:16` aliases `server-only` to a stub, so **Vitest cannot catch this violation**. Only `pnpm build` can. Recorded under "what the harness cannot cover".

## Data flow

    src/app/layout.tsx  (async Server Component)
      await getProducts()                    <- server-only, stays on the server
      toCartCatalog(products)   -> CartCatalog      (plain data)
      await getPricingPolicy()  -> { transferRateBp }  (plain number)
        |
        v  serializable props only [V] use-client.md:50
    <CartProvider catalog={...} transferRateBp={1000}>   'use client'
        useReducer(cartReducer)          <- pure, TDD-able
        mount effect: storage.read() -> reconcile(stored, index) -> dispatch('rehydrate')
        write effect: keyed on lines AND notices; skipped while hydration === 'pending'
        checkout = createLocalCheckout(catalog)
        |
        +-- CartStateContext    (lines, hydration, notices)
        +-- CartDispatchContext (dispatch — stable identity)
        |
        v
    ui/  trigger+badge | drawer/sheet | line row | stepper | summary | notices | empty
                                                      |
                                                 useCheckout(port)  idle -> pending -> settled

## Architecture decisions

### D1. Catalog reaches the client as a narrow projection, not `ProductView[]`

| Option | Tradeoff | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Client calls `CatalogPort` | impossible — `server-only` build error **[V]** `:580` | Rejected (not viable) |
| Second client-safe catalog entry point without `server-only` | forks the module boundary and defeats the token guard the marker exists for | Rejected |
| Reconcile on the server | localStorage is client-only; the server cannot see the persisted cart | Rejected |
| **`CartCatalog` projection passed from `layout.tsx`** | couples the root layout to the catalog; costs an RSC payload | **Adopt** |

`CartCatalog = Array<{ productId; slug; title; image: string \| null; variants: Array<{ id; combination: string[]; price: Money; inStock: boolean }> }>`.

Deliberately **excludes `descriptionHtml`**, `axes`, `compareAt`, `tags` — same reasoning the storefront design applied to `PurchasePanel` ("receives `{axes, variants}`, not the whole `ProductView`"). Built by `toCartCatalog(products: ProductView[]): CartCatalog` in `cart/domain/catalog-projection.ts`: the cart depends on catalog **types**, the catalog never learns the cart exists.

**Honest cost, named**: the cart makes the root layout a catalog consumer. Today `getProducts()` is a synchronous fixture scan **[V]** `source.ts:27-31`, so nothing changes. With a live Tiendanube source it becomes a per-request network call on **every route**, under a leaky-bucket rate limit **[V]** `port.ts:31-34`. Caching the snapshot is real, unbuilt work. This does **not** swap cleanly.

### D2. Pricing policy — port for the value, pure function for the arithmetic

Binding answer 1: 10% is fixed brand policy but lives as a Tiendanube store setting; the rate must not be a constant read at call sites.

The proposal's `catalog/lib/pricing.ts` exporting `TRANSFER_DISCOUNT_RATE` **does not survive that answer** — an exported constant *is* the call-site constant. **Location kept, content split:**

| File | Contents | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `catalog/api/pricing.ts` (private) | `PricingPolicyPort { getPricingPolicy(): Promise<PricingPolicy> \| PricingPolicy }`, plus today's local implementation returning `{ transferRateBp: 1000 }` | store settings arrive through the same admin API, same token, same rate limit as products — the same port shape as `CatalogPort` **[V]** `port.ts:14-19` |
| `catalog/lib/pricing.ts` (pure) | `applyRate(m: Money, bp: number): Money`, `transferBreakdown(subtotal, bp): { discount, total }` | `Money` arithmetic, next to `money.ts` **[V]** |
| `catalog/index.ts` | re-export `getPricingPolicy` + the two pure functions + `PricingPolicy` | one barrel, both consumers (PDP `PriceBlock` and cart summary) |

Rejected: a new `pricing` module (ceremony at 3 SKUs); cart-owned rate (guarantees PDP/cart drift); a bare parameterised function with no provider (relocates the constant to call sites — the exact thing answer 1 forbids).

**Rate representation: integer basis points, not a float.** 10% = `1000` bp. `discount = Math.round(subtotal.amount * bp / 10_000)` — integer multiply, one divide, one rounding. A `0.10` float multiplied into minor units reintroduces precisely the error `money.ts` is hand-rolled to avoid **[V]** `money.ts:31-37`. Applied **once to the subtotal**, never per line: 3 × 27000_00 = 81000_00 → −8100_00 → 72900_00, matching the artboards exactly.

**Rate delivery: resolved on the server, passed as a `number` prop.** Serializable **[V]** `use-client.md:50`, keeps every pricing component synchronous and Vitest-testable, and moves the future fetch onto the already-async server boundary. Rejected: resolving it in a client effect — that would make the *total* arrive after paint, which is worse than the badge flash.

**Stacking (answer 3) needs no new code.** **[V]** `map.ts:69-75` already puts `promotional_price` into `VariantView.price` and the original into `compareAt`. The cart uses `variant.price`, so the transfer rate already applies to the current effective price. This is a rule to **test**, not to implement.

### D3. Persistence stores identity, a price witness, and pending notices — never live display data

`localStorage` key `flesh.cart.v1`; payload:

```ts
const StoredCartSchema = z.object({
  v: z.literal(1),
  lines: z.array(z.object({
    productId: z.number().int(),
    variantId: z.number().int(),
    quantity: z.number().int().positive(),
    unitPriceMinor: z.number().int(),
    currency: z.string(),
  })),
  // Defaulted, not required: a payload written by an earlier build of this
  // same change decodes cleanly instead of being discarded as invalid.
  notices: z.array(StoredNoticeSchema).default([]),
});
```

| Persisted | Not persisted | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `productId`, `variantId`, `quantity` | `title`, `image`, `combination` for **lines** | catalog is the single source of truth for a live line's display; persisted copies would render stale with no policy for "the product was renamed" |
| `unitPriceMinor` + `currency` as a **witness** | — | price drift is undetectable without the last-shown price. **Never used for arithmetic or display** — only for the drift comparison |
| **pending `notices`, including their `item` label** | — | see D4 — a notice is a record of an event that already happened, so it carries its own text; it is not a view onto anything still live |

**Why notices persist at all**: the reconciled lines are written back immediately, so the drift that produced a notice is *gone from storage* by the next load. Holding the notice only in provider state means it survives soft navigation (the React tree is preserved) but dies on a hard reload — and the visitor would open an unexplained empty cart. The notice must outlive the fact it describes, so it is stored with it.

**Version stays `v: 1`.** Nothing has ever been persisted by a shipped build, so this is not a migration; and `notices` is `.default([])` so intra-change forward compatibility costs nothing. Version is still carried **twice** — in the key (an incompatible future shape is simply not found: safe silent reset) and in the payload (a compatible migration can be written).

**Record lifetime**: the write effect is keyed on **lines and notices**, and the storage record is deleted only when **both** are empty. An empty cart holding a pending notice is a legitimate persisted state — that is exactly the "even if that leaves the cart empty" case.

`CartStoragePort { read(): StoredCart \| null; write(c: StoredCart): void; clear(): void }` — **synchronous**, unlike `CheckoutPort`. The asymmetry is deliberate: checkout's destination is known to be a network call, storage's is not (a server-side cart would arrive through `CheckoutPort`/`CatalogPort`, not through this). Inventing async here would be cargo-culting the other port's rationale.

Decoding is **Zod**, not a cast — `localStorage` is user-editable, i.e. attacker-controlled input, the same situation `catalog/api/schema.ts` already handles at the wire boundary; zod 4 is already a dependency **[V]** `package.json:25`. Every access is wrapped in `try/catch`: `localStorage` can throw on quota and when storage is blocked, and a cart is not worth crashing a page over **[J]**. Failure → treated as absent.

### D4. Reconciliation — pure, synchronous, one dispatch; drift removes the line and notifies

`reconcile(stored: StoredCart, index: Map<variantId, {product, variant}>): { lines: CartLine[]; notices: CartNotice[] }` in `cart/domain/reconcile.ts`. **Zero IO.** The effect does the IO (read storage, build the index from the prop); the effect then dispatches exactly one `rehydrate` action carrying the pure result.

**It is synchronous** — the catalog was already resolved on the server (D1). The proposal assumed async because **[V]** `port.ts:15` returns a `Promise | value` union; that resolution now happens above the client boundary.

**Settled by the user (binding, not reopened here):** an out-of-stock variant's line is **removed automatically during rehydration** and the visitor is **notified** that it was removed and why. There is no kept-but-marked line, and no CTA block. The cost was stated to the user and accepted: the visitor loses the item without ever seeing it in the cart.

**Orchestrator judgment, overturnable by the user:** the vanished-variant case is **also notified**, not silently dropped. The persistence shape (D3) constrains what a notice can *name*, not whether one is *emitted*; and from the visitor's side "gone from the catalog" and "out of stock" are the same event — their item disappeared. Notifying about one and staying silent about the other would be arbitrary. The proposal's silent-drop rule predates the existence of any notice mechanism.

| Drift | Detection | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| Variant out of stock | `variant.inStock === false` **[V]** `product.ts:34` | **remove the line**, emit a **named** `removed` notice (`reason: "out-of-stock"`) |
| Variant/product no longer exists | absent from the index | **remove the line**, emit an **unnamed** `removed` notice (`reason: "unknown-variant"`) |
| Price changed | `variant.price.amount !== unitPriceMinor` | keep, **reprice to the catalog price**, emit a `repriced` notice with before/after |

**The notice degrades honestly, and the asymmetry is deliberate, not hidden:**

```ts
type CartNotice =
  | { kind: "removed"; reason: "out-of-stock";    variantId: CartLineId; item: string }
  | { kind: "removed"; reason: "unknown-variant"; variantId: CartLineId; item: null }
  | { kind: "repriced"; variantId: CartLineId; item: string; from: Money; to: Money };
```

`item` is non-null **exactly when the catalog can still rebuild the label** — out-of-stock and repriced lines are present in the index, so `"<title> / <combination>"` is available; a vanished variant is not, and D3 deliberately persisted no title for lines to fall back on. So the two copies differ in specificity, and the type makes that a compile-time fact rather than a runtime `?? "un producto"`. A caller cannot accidentally render an empty name.

**Persisted notices carry `item`; they do not re-derive it.** Two reasons, and the second is the load-bearing one:

1. `reason: "unknown-variant"` has **nothing to re-derive from** — the variant is absent from the catalog and D3 persists no line display data. If the label were derived at render time this notice could never be named, and worse, it could not even be reconstructed as a *specific* notice. The persisted copy is the only surviving trace of the event.
2. Deriving the label for the other kinds while persisting it for this one would create two code paths and let a notice silently change its text if the merchant renames a product between sessions. A notice is a **record of what the visitor was told**, in the same sense `unitPriceMinor` is a record of the price they were shown. Same discipline, same reason.

This is the one place display text is persisted, and it is persisted precisely because it is *not* a view onto live data.

`StoredNotice` mirrors the union with `Money` flattened to minor units, and is Zod-decoded like the rest of the payload:

```ts
const StoredNoticeSchema = z.discriminatedUnion("kind", [
  z.object({ kind: z.literal("removed"),
             reason: z.enum(["out-of-stock", "unknown-variant"]),
             variantId: z.number().int(),
             item: z.string().nullable() }),
  z.object({ kind: z.literal("repriced"), variantId: z.number().int(),
             item: z.string(),
             fromMinor: z.number().int(), toMinor: z.number().int(),
             currency: z.string() }),
]);
```

**Notice identity is `variantId`** — a variant's line is either removed or repriced, never both, so no synthetic id is needed. Same reasoning that made `CartLineId` the variant id.

**Rehydration merges notices, it does not replace them.** `reconcile` returns freshly-detected notices; the effect merges them with the still-pending persisted ones, keyed by `variantId`, **fresh wins on collision** (it describes the more recent observation). Without the merge, a second reload before the visitor opens the cart would wipe a notice that was never seen — the exact failure this decision exists to close.

**`dismissNotice` must reach storage.** Because the write effect is keyed on notices as well as lines (D3), dismissal persists automatically: the notice leaves provider state, the record is rewritten without it, and it does not return on the next load. This is *why* the write effect keys on notices — if it keyed only on lines, dismissal would be purely cosmetic and the notice would resurrect on every reload.

**Revised invariant.** Notices are **produced** only by `rehydrate` — no other action creates one, and that still holds. But they are now also **restored** from storage on the same path, and **removed** by `dismissNotice`. Production, restoration and dismissal are three distinct paths; only the first is a judgment about catalog drift.

**Totals contain only buyable lines by construction.** Because unavailable lines never survive reconciliation, no selector needs an availability filter and the summary cannot display a total the visitor is unable to pay. This is a simplification the removal policy buys.

**Three ordering hazards, decided:**

1. **Read must be in an effect, not a `useState` initializer.** The provider also renders on the server, where `window` is undefined; a lazy initializer would produce a hydration mismatch. The empty-first-paint cost (badge flashes empty) is accepted, as in the proposal.
2. **The write effect is skipped while `hydration === 'pending'`.** Otherwise the empty initial state overwrites the stored cart — and now also its pending notices — before either is ever read. This is the classic localStorage-provider bug; it is named here so it is designed out rather than debugged later.
3. **`rehydrate` merges, it does not replace.** A click landing between mount and the effect would otherwise be clobbered. Merge uses the same rule as `add` (same `variantId` → quantities sum), so the reducer stays pure and the race is covered by a unit test rather than by timing.

**Hydration is two states, not three**: `'pending' | 'ready'`. Reconcile is sync, so there is no observable restoring phase.

### D5. `CheckoutPort` — final shape, and what `rejected` is worth now

```ts
// src/modules/cart/api/port.ts
export type CartLineId = VariantView["id"];   // the variant id IS the line key

export type CheckoutOutcome =
  | { status: "redirect"; url: string }
  | { status: "rejected"; lines: CartLineId[] }
  | { status: "unavailable"; reason: string };

export interface CheckoutPort {
  startCheckout(cart: CartView): Promise<CheckoutOutcome>;
}

export function createLocalCheckout(catalog: CartCatalog): CheckoutPort;
```

`CartLineId` is the variant id, not a synthetic key — the same reasoning the storefront design used to reject a synthetic axis/value linking key, and it is the id a real Tiendanube order references.

**`createLocalCheckout` is a factory, not a module singleton.** It closes over the `CartCatalog` because it cannot import the catalog (D1), and that closure is simultaneously the test seam.

**Local implementation, in order**: re-run the availability check against the catalog → if any line is unavailable, return `rejected` with those ids → otherwise return `unavailable`. The ordering mirrors what the live implementation must do (a real checkout rejects on stock before creating a session), and with in-stock fixtures the observable behaviour is still `unavailable`, satisfying binding answer 2. **The CTA is never blocked client-side** — it always calls the port and renders whatever comes back.

**Honest limit, and it got sharper under D4.** Removing unavailable lines at rehydration means that within a session no line can be unavailable at checkout time: the snapshot is fixed for the page's lifetime and the PDP only offers in-stock variants. So `rejected` is now **unreachable through the UI** and is exercised only by unit tests against a synthetic catalog. It keeps a real producer in code and a proven call path; it does not have a live one. Only a server holding independent stock truth gives it a genuine trigger.

### D6. Pending state — an explicit machine, not `isPending`

`useCheckout(port)` in `cart/state/use-checkout.ts`:

```ts
type CheckoutUiState =
  | { phase: "idle" }
  | { phase: "pending" }
  | { phase: "settled"; outcome: CheckoutOutcome };
```

| Option | Tradeoff | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `useTransition` / `isPending` **[V]** `07-mutating-data.md:561-575` | the documented Next pending mechanism, but a **boolean cannot hold the outcome** — the `unavailable` message must persist on screen after settling | Rejected as source of truth; **recorded as the upgrade** for the day `startCheckout` becomes a Server Function |
| CTA `disabled` only | no place for the outcome at all | Rejected |
| **Explicit 3-phase machine** | ~20 lines; deterministic and testable | **Adopt** |

`phase: "pending"` is set **synchronously before the await**. Today's port resolves immediately, so React may batch pending and settled into a single commit and **the pending frame may never paint**. That is correct and stated plainly: the machine exists and is exercised, and it will produce a visible frame the day the port does real IO. **Padding with `setTimeout` to make the spinner visible is rejected** — faking latency to demo a loading state is the dishonesty this whole seam exists to avoid.

The pending phase is made **observable in tests** by injecting a deferred fake port. This is the reason port injection is a design requirement, not a convenience.

**Injection constraint, verified**: `CartProvider` accepts `checkout?: CheckoutPort` — **optional, and never supplied from a Server Component**. **[V]** `use-client.md:50-56` — functions are not serializable across the server→client boundary. `layout.tsx` passes only `catalog` and `transferRateBp` (plain data); tests render the provider from client code, where a function prop is fine. Written down because the failure is a runtime serialization error at the exact boundary.

Re-entrancy: the CTA is `disabled` while `pending` and the hook ignores re-entrant calls. No request-id bookkeeping at this scale.

### D7. State — Context + `useReducer`, split. Confirmed, on different grounds

**[V]** `05-server-and-client-components.md:352-397` prescribes exactly this shape: a `'use client'` provider taking `children`, imported into a Server Component layout. **[V]** `use-client.md:14` — directive at the top of the file, before imports.

The split into `CartStateContext` and `CartDispatchContext` is **confirmed, but the proposal's justification is downgraded**. **[V]** `reactCompiler.md:6`: the compiler "reduces the need for manual memoization" — it does not change context propagation, so the re-render argument is technically true **[J]**, but at 3 SKUs and ≤6 lines it is worth nothing.

**The real reason is encapsulation, matching the module boundary rule**: a component importing `useCartDispatch` *cannot read totals*, and one importing `useCartState` *cannot mutate*. "Who can change the cart" becomes a type-level fact. The PDP add-to-cart button and the header trigger sit on opposite sides of that line.

Rejected, unchanged from the proposal: `useSyncExternalStore` (buys non-React reads nothing needs, forces a `getServerSnapshot`); a store library (**[V]** `package.json` has none and the surface has been kept deliberately empty); cookies/Server Actions for the stepper (no server, and dynamic rendering on every route for a cosmetic gain).

Reducer actions: `add | increment | decrement | remove | clear | rehydrate | dismissNotice`. `add` merges on `variantId`; `decrement` below 1 removes. **No `setQuantity`** — the artboards show a stepper and `QUITAR`, no free-text input; inventing one is UI redesign.

### D8. ESLint — a second config object, and why widening `ignores` is not an option

```js
{
  files: ["**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,mjs}"],
  ignores: ["src/modules/cart/**"],
  rules: { "no-restricted-imports": ["error", { patterns: [{ group: [
    "**/modules/cart/api", "**/modules/cart/api/**",
    "**/cart/api", "**/cart/api/**",
  ], message: "..." }] }] },
}
```

**[V]** `eslint.config.mjs:25-47`: in flat config, `ignores` scopes **the object it sits in**, not the file globally. Widening the existing object to `ignores: ["src/modules/catalog/**", "src/modules/cart/**"]` would exempt cart files from the **catalog** rule — so `src/modules/cart/state/provider.tsx` could deep-import `@/modules/catalog/api/types`, pull `{en,es,pt}` objects and price strings into the cart, and `pnpm lint` would stay green. The cart would silently defeat the exact rule it is copying, and symmetrically the catalog would be exempt from the cart rule. **Each module exempts only itself.** This is the whole reason the shape is non-negotiable.

Accepted asymmetry: like catalog, only `api/**` is sealed. `state/**` and `ui/**` rely on the barrel convention.

## File changes

| File | Action | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `src/modules/cart/api/port.ts` | Create | `CheckoutPort`, `CheckoutOutcome`, `CartLineId` |
| `src/modules/cart/api/checkout.local.ts` | Create | `createLocalCheckout(catalog)` — reject-then-unavailable |
| `src/modules/cart/api/storage.ts` | Create | `CartStoragePort`, `StoredCart`/`StoredNotice` zod schemas, localStorage adapter |
| `src/modules/cart/domain/line.ts` | Create | `CartLine`, `CartView`, `CartNotice`, `CartTotals` |
| `src/modules/cart/domain/reducer.ts` | Create | pure `cartReducer` + `CartAction` (incl. notice merge + dismissal) |
| `src/modules/cart/domain/selectors.ts` | Create | `itemCount`, `subtotal`, `totals(lines, bp)` |
| `src/modules/cart/domain/reconcile.ts` | Create | pure drift reconciliation + notice production/merge |
| `src/modules/cart/domain/catalog-projection.ts` | Create | `toCartCatalog(ProductView[])`, index builder |
| `src/modules/cart/state/cart-context.tsx` | Create | `'use client'` — two contexts, provider, hooks |
| `src/modules/cart/state/use-checkout.ts` | Create | `'use client'` — idle/pending/settled machine |
| `src/modules/cart/ui/*.tsx` | Create | trigger, drawer/sheet, line row, stepper, summary, notices, empty |
| `src/modules/cart/index.ts` | Create | the one crossing point |
| `src/modules/catalog/api/pricing.ts` | Create | `PricingPolicyPort` + local implementation |
| `src/modules/catalog/lib/pricing.ts` | Create | `applyRate`, `transferBreakdown` (basis points) |
| `src/modules/catalog/index.ts` | Modify | re-export pricing policy + pure helpers |
| `eslint.config.mjs` | Modify | second config object sealing `cart/api/**` |
| `src/app/layout.tsx` | Modify | resolve catalog projection + rate, mount `CartProvider` |
| Header (storefront PR5b) | Modify | cart trigger + count badge |
| `PurchasePanel` (storefront PR8a) | Modify | add-to-cart dispatches — **supersedes task 8a.3's inert assertion** |
| `next.config.ts` | Unchanged | `reactCompiler` on **[V]** `:5`, `cacheComponents` absent |

## Testing strategy

Harness **[V]** `sdd/flesh/testing-capabilities`: Vitest 4 `jsdom`, RTL 16, `pnpm test | typecheck | lint`, 11 files / 60 tests green.

| Layer | What | Approach |
|---|---|---|
| Pure unit (no DOM) | reducer: add / merge-same-variant / increment / decrement-to-removal / clear / **rehydrate merge with a mid-flight add** / **`dismissNotice` removes exactly one notice by `variantId`**; selectors incl. the 81000→8100→72900 artboard case; `applyRate`/`transferBreakdown` in basis points and the promo-stacking rule (D2); **`reconcile`: out-of-stock removal + named notice, unknown-variant removal + unnamed notice, reprice + before/after notice, all three combined in one cart, and the notice merge (persisted pending + freshly detected, fresh wins on `variantId` collision)**; `toCartCatalog` projection; `createLocalCheckout` returning `rejected` (synthetic catalog) then `unavailable` | plain Vitest — this is where the risk lives, and it needs no React |
| Codec (jsdom, no RTL) | storage encode/decode round-trip for lines **and notices** (both `removed` reasons, `repriced` with minor-unit `from`/`to`); **notice persisted → simulated reload → still present** (the hard-reload case that motivates D3); **notice dismissed → written back → simulated reload → gone**; **empty lines + pending notice keeps the record; both empty deletes it**; payload without `notices` decodes via `.default([])`; unknown `v`, malformed JSON, schema-invalid payload, throwing `localStorage` | real `window.localStorage` + a throwing stub; "reload" = discard the provider and re-read storage |
| RTL | provider add→badge count, stepper ±, remove, drawer open/close + focus, empty state, **notice rendering for both `removed` reasons and for `repriced`**, **dismissal removes it from the DOM**, **CTA idle→pending→settled driven by a deferred fake `CheckoutPort`** | RTL + injected port; the deferred port is what makes `pending` observable |
| Not coverable by this harness | drawer-vs-sheet responsive split (jsdom has no viewport); SSR/hydration mismatch and the empty-first-paint flash (no SSR pass); **`server-only` leakage into the client graph — [V] `vitest.config.mts:16` aliases it to a stub, so the unit suite is structurally blind to this class of error and only `pnpm build` catches it**; real checkout behaviour (no server); a genuine browser reload (only simulated above); focus-trap/scroll-lock fidelity | manual + `pnpm build`; Playwright stays deferred, consistent with `sdd/flesh-storefront/design` |

Strict TDD: RED first everywhere. The pure-unit column is the opening slice and needs no UI to exist.

## Threat matrix

Reference matrix rows (routing/shell/subprocess/VCS/PR/executable classification): **all N/A** — this change adds no shell commands, subprocesses, VCS or PR automation, and no file classification or process integration.

Applicable input boundaries, carried to tasks as RED tests:

| Boundary | Applicable | Expected behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `localStorage` payload is user-editable, attacker-controlled input | **Yes** | Zod-validated on read; malformed / wrong-version / hostile payloads are treated as absent and cleared, never trusted, never thrown out of the provider |
| Injected `variantId`/`productId` from storage | **Yes** | only ever used as a lookup key into the in-memory catalog index; an unknown id removes the line and emits an unnamed notice — never touches fs, path or network |
| Persisted quantity | **Yes** | clamped to a positive integer on decode; a negative or non-integer quantity must not reach the totals |
| **Persisted `notices`, including the `item` label** | **Yes** | the one persisted display string in the payload, and therefore attacker-controlled: `StoredNoticeSchema` decodes it as a plain `string`, the UI renders it **as text only**, never as HTML. The cart has no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` call site and `descriptionHtml` is excluded from `CartCatalog` (D1), so there is no route from a forged notice to markup execution. A forged or oversized `item` can only produce misleading copy, never script |
| Persisted `repriced` amounts | **Yes** | decoded as integers and used only to render the notice's before/after — never fed into `transferBreakdown` or any total, which always recompute from the catalog price |

## What still does not swap cleanly

Carried forward from the proposal, unlaundered, plus one new item:

1. **There is no server.** A live checkout needs a `'use server'` module or Route Handler plus env/secret handling. Not scaffolded here.
2. **Variant ids are hand-authored fixtures.** Persisted carts reference ids that do not exist in a real store; the first live deploy invalidates every stored cart. Mitigation is only that `reconcile` removes them and says so.
3. **Reconciliation is local-only.** It compares against the same snapshot the UI already rendered, so it can detect fixture drift but never real stock or price truth.
4. **The store URL / `store_id` is still unknown** (binding answer 4). Blocks the live implementation, not this change.
5. **NEW — the root layout becomes a catalog consumer** (D1). Free today (sync fixtures), a per-route fetch under a rate limit tomorrow. Caching the projection is unbuilt work.

## Risks

- **Recorded tradeoff, settled and not reopened**: removing an out-of-stock line during rehydration means the visitor never sees the item they chose in the cart — a notice is the only trace, which is why D3/D4 make that notice survive a reload and only disappear on explicit dismissal.
- A persisted notice's `item` label is frozen at detection time, so a product renamed between sessions will be announced under its old name. Accepted: a notice is a record of what the visitor was told, not a live view.
- `CheckoutOutcome.rejected` has a producer and unit coverage but **no reachable UI path** once unavailable lines are removed at rehydration (D5). It stays in the type so the live implementation has a branch to return, not because anything exercises it in the product.
- Reconciliation runs once per mount against a snapshot frozen for the page's lifetime; drift occurring *during* a session is invisible until the next load.
- **The drawer has a fixed height and notices compete with line items for it.** Measured while building the notice artboards: three notices plus three line items overflow the 936px desktop drawer by ~110px and collapse the bottom spacer. The line-item area must scroll; mobile at 390px is tighter still.

## Migration / rollout

No data migration; nothing has been persisted by a shipped build. Storage stays at `v: 1`, with `notices` decoded via `.default([])` so payloads written by an earlier slice of this same change survive. Slices 1–2 have no consumers (delete the directory + revert two lines to restore the tree); slice 4 reverting restores the inert CTA and removes the trigger. `git revert` per slice, feature-branch chain.

## Open questions

- [x] **RESOLVED by the orchestrator — the notice region now exists.** Two artboards were added to the pen.dev document: `Cart / Desktop - Avisos` (all three notice kinds at once) and `Cart / Desktop - Vacio con aviso` (the notice surviving over an emptied cart, i.e. the D3 record-lifetime case). Treatment, reusing existing motifs rather than inventing UI: no boxes or cards; an 8px square marker (the same motif as the PDP's FIT marker), body-font text at 13px with `$tracking-control`, an `x` dismiss icon in `$muted-foreground`, and rows separated by 1px `$border` rules. Marker colour carries the kind — `$destructive` for both removal reasons, `$foreground` for `repriced` — so the kinds are distinguishable without reading. **Still open: the mobile variant.** At 390px the same copy wraps to three or four lines, so the height ceiling is tighter there. *(The previously-flagged "unavailable line item" visual is no longer needed: removed lines are not drawn.)*
- [x] **RESOLVED — accents ARE allowed in notice copy.** Verified against `app/layout.tsx:14-21`: Copperplate Gothic Std 30 AB declares **no** `unicode-range`, and that is a measurement, not an oversight — `fc-query` reports `20-7e a0-ff 131 141-142 152-153 ...`, and `a0-ff` covers á é í ó ú ñ ¿ ¡. The body voice renders the whole Spanish set on its own. Only **display-font** (`$font-display`, Kraut) strings remain ASCII-only, per its measured `U+0020-007E, U+E000-E001` declared at `layout.tsx:44`. Notices are body copy, so accented copy is correct. Avoid characters outside Latin-1 (em dash, curly quotes) — those fall outside the measured range.
- [ ] Confirm the `PricingPolicyPort` return shape (`{ transferRateBp }`) survives contact with the real Tiendanube store-settings payload, which nobody has seen yet.

Per design's testing strategy "not coverable by this harness": drawer-vs-sheet responsive split, SSR/hydration mismatch and the empty-first-paint flash, a genuine browser reload, and focus-trap/scroll-lock fidelity all require manual verification or a deferred Playwright pass — no task above claims to close them with `pnpm test`.

Also not covered by this change: the mobile variant of the notice region (artboards cover desktop only), and confirming `PricingPolicyPort`'s `{ transferRateBp }` shape against the real Tiendanube store-settings payload.

observations.title: flesh-cart: entrega en 8 PRs encadenados, sin excepciones de tamaño
observations.content:
**What**: Decisión de entrega del change `flesh-cart` (2026-08-31), tomada en el review workload guard con `delivery_strategy: ask-on-risk`.

**8 unidades de trabajo encadenadas** bajo un tracker `flesh-cart`, en `feature-branch-chain`: PR1a, 1b, 1c (dominio puro), 2a, 2b (storage y provider), 3a, 3b (UI), 4 (integración). Ningún PR pasa las 400 líneas, así que **no se marca `size:exception` en ninguno**.

Descartado: los 4 slices originales del design con excepción en cada uno, y subir el presupuesto de revisión.

**Why**: El forecast dio 1600–2200 líneas contra un presupuesto de 400, riesgo Alto. Los 4 slices del design individualmente pasaban las 400 una vez contados los tests RED-first — `reconcile.ts` solo necesita cinco escenarios. El usuario priorizó que cada PR se revise de verdad por encima de la ceremonia de abrir y mergear ocho.

**Where**: `sdd/flesh-cart/tasks` (obs #33). Cadena de planificación completa: explore → proposal → spec → design → tasks.

**Learned**:
- **El estimado se duplicó respecto del proposal (700–1200 → 1600–2200), y la causa es identificable**: el amendment de persistencia de avisos (design D3/D4). La unión de tipos `CartNotice`, su codec Zod, el merge en rehidratación y el descarte que escribe a storage no existían en el proposal. La decisión de "eliminar y avisar" resultó bastante más cara de lo que aparentaba cuando se tomó.

observations.title: Session summary: flesh
observations.content:
Sesión: diseño visual del carrito FLESH + planificación SDD completa del change `flesh-cart`.

**Diseño (pen.dev, documento del GATE)**. Cuatro artboards de carrito: `Cart / Desktop` (drawer derecho de 520px con scrim), `Cart / Desktop - Vacio`, `Cart / Mobile` (sheet full-bleed 390x844), `Cart Entry / Header States`. Después, dos más para cubrir un hueco que destapó la fase de design: `Cart / Desktop - Avisos` y `Cart / Desktop - Vacio con aviso`. Se eligió drawer sobre página dedicada porque el sitio no tiene barra de nav — el header es sólo el wordmark centrado. Hallazgo al construirlo: tres avisos más tres líneas desbordan el drawer de 936px por ~110px; las líneas tienen que scrollear. Falta la variante mobile de avisos.

**SDD `flesh-cart`, cadena completa**: explore (#25) → proposal (#28) → spec (#30) → design (#32) → tasks (#33). Preflight: interactive, engram, ask-on-risk, 400 líneas.

**Decisiones de producto del usuario**:
- Checkout: **integración real con la API de Tiendanube** como target, pero este change hace **sólo la capa visual + dominio**, con el seam armado.
- Orden **estrictamente secuencial**: `flesh-storefront` primero.
- Deriva del catálogo al rehidratar: sin stock → **eliminar + avisar**; precio cambiado → **adoptar el nuevo + avisar**; variante inexistente → eliminar + avisar (unificado por juicio del orquestador).
- Tasa de transferencia: política fija de marca pero **inyectable**, porque el valor vive como setting de tienda.
- Entrega: **8 PRs encadenados**, sin `size:exception`.

**Hallazgos técnicos verificados**:
1. **Tiendanube NO soporta deeplink de carrito.** El add-to-cart es `<form method="post">` con `add_to_cart` de valor único — un producto por submit. Verificado contra `TiendaNube/base-theme` master. Mató la opción de checkout que el usuario había elegido primero.
2. **`@/modules/catalog` es inalcanzable desde código de cliente.** `source.ts:7` lleva `import "server-only"` y `index.ts:14` lo re-exporta como valor. Reordenó el diseño entero: el catálogo se proyecta desde el layout servidor y la reconciliación queda pura y sincrónica.
3. **La suite de tests es ciega a esa clase de error.** `vitest.config.mts:16` aliasea `server-only` a un stub. Sólo `pnpm build` la agarra.
4. **El descuento por transferencia no tiene modelo de datos.** `promotional_price` modela una promoción de producto, no un descuento por medio de pago. Agujero cruzado: afecta también al `PriceBlock` de la PDP en `flesh-storefront` PR8a, que no lo tiene en su lista de tareas.
5. Copperplate cubre `a0-ff`, así que los avisos pueden llevar tildes; sólo Kraut está limitada a ASCII.
6. Memoria de testing capabilities corregida: decía "sin runner", hay 60 tests pasando.

**Estado**: `sdd-apply` BLOQUEADO por el gate de orden — `app/page.tsx` sigue siendo el default de create-next-app. El trabajo real que sigue es `flesh-storefront` PR5a/5b/7/8a.

**Pendientes abiertos**: URL/`store_id` de la tienda Tiendanube (sin conseguir), forma del payload de settings para `PricingPolicyPort`, variante mobile de avisos. Basura pegada en un comentario de `app/layout.tsx:11` y `metadata` con los defaults de create-next-app.

observations.title: Repo flesh en GitHub: privado, y necesita el alias SSH github.com-personal
observations.content:
**What**: El repo `flesh` se publicó en GitHub el 2026-08-31 y quedó **PRIVADO**.

- URL: `https://github.com/FelipeS02/flesh`
- Remote configurado: `git@github.com-personal:FelipeS02/flesh.git` — **NO** `git@github.com:...`
- Branch por defecto: `main`
- Se subieron las 7 ramas: `main`, `feature/flesh-storefront` (tracker), `pr1-vitest-harness`, `pr2-design-tokens`, `pr4a-catalog-contract`, `pr4b-catalog-domain`, `pr4c-catalog-sanitize`.

**Why — el gotcha del alias SSH, que cuesta 10 minutos si no se sabe**: esta máquina tiene DOS identidades de GitHub. El host SSH por defecto `github.com` usa `~/.ssh/github` y autentica como **`felipe-itrock`** (cuenta de trabajo). El repo es de **`FelipeS02`** (cuenta personal), cuya clave está en `~/.ssh/github_personal`, expuesta por el alias `github.com-personal` ya presente en `~/.ssh/config`.

Un `git remote add origin git@github.com:FelipeS02/flesh.git` falla con `Permission to FelipeS02/flesh.git denied to felipe-itrock`. La solución es el alias, y se aplicó **sólo a este repo** — el `~/.ssh/config` global quedó intacto para no romper los repos de trabajo. `gh` ya está logueado en ambas cuentas, con FelipeS02 como activa.

**Where**: `.git/config` de `/Users/felipesaracho/proyectos/flesh`.

**Learned**:
- **Estado real de las ramas al momento de subir**: `main` y el tracker `feature/flesh-storefront` están los dos todavía en `f2090e0` (initial commit de create-next-app). **Nada está mergeado.** Los 12 commits de trabajo viven en una cadena lineal sana sobre `pr2-design-tokens`: PR1 → PR4a → PR4b → PR4c → PR2. Verificado con `git merge-base --is-ancestor`: cada rama es ancestro de la siguiente.
- Commit `dda4e71` agregó `.atl/` y `src/assets/` a `pr2-design-tokens`.
- **Por qué se puso privado**: el repo nació público y hay dos binarios de fuente commiteados en `app/fonts/` — `copperplate-gothic-30ab.ttf` (Adobe, comercial) y `kraut.ttf` (licencia indeterminada). El usuario había aceptado el riesgo de USARLAS en el sitio, pero publicar el binario en un repo público es redistribución, que es un problema distinto y más claro. Privado lo resuelve sin reescribir historia.
- **Los assets de `src/assets/` son mocks y NO llegan a producción** (confirmado por el usuario). `3.webp` y `4.webp` son fotos de otra marca (rotten) usadas de placeholder. Como el repo es privado, no hace falta sacarlos del historial — pero tampoco deben terminar en un deploy público.
- **Si el repo se vuelve público en el futuro**, las fuentes y los webp siguen en el historial de Git desde el primer push. Borrarlos en un commit nuevo no los saca; hay que reescribir historia y forzar el push.
- Se revirtió antes de subir un token basura (`VYgd55s%mUc3TcdNTthn`) que estaba pegado sin commitear en un comentario de `app/layout.tsx:11`. No llegó al repo.

observations.title: El ledger de sdd-attempt derivó 4 slices y necesitó reset autorizado
observations.content:
**What**: Al arrancar PR5b (2026-09-01) el ledger nativo `gentle-ai sdd-attempt` estaba bloqueado. Su objetivo activo seguía siendo la generación 3 (`PR4b-mapper-money-locale-selectors`) con el intento en `outcome: running`, nunca cerrado — mientras PR4b, PR4c, PR2 y PR5a se implementaron y committearon fuera del ledger.

Secuencia real de recuperación:
1. `acquire` para PR5b → `blocked / active_attempt`, devuelve el token del intento viejo.
2. `settle --outcome passed` de ese token → `blocked / maintainer_decision`. Motivo: el intento arrancó en el árbol de PR4a (`74d26d25`) y HEAD ya era `f720445`, así que el diff medido (8985 líneas) reventó el presupuesto de 600. No fue fallo de ejecución, fue deriva de bookkeeping.
3. `reset` con `--expected-revision`, `--actor felipesaracho02@gmail.com` — **autorización explícita del usuario, el reset nunca es automático**. Primer intento falló por conflicto de revisión (mi `settle` fallido ya había bumpeado la revisión); el error imprime la revisión correcta para reintentar.
4. El reset absorbió el settle: el intento 3 quedó registrado como `passed` con su evidencia real, y el ledger pasó a `next_action: begin`.
5. `acquire` con presupuesto 2500 líneas → `state: proceed`.

**Why**: Que un slice termine y se committee NO cierra su intento en el ledger. El cierre es una llamada explícita.

**Where**: `gentle-ai sdd-attempt {acquire,status,settle,reset}` sobre `/Users/felipesaracho/proyectos/flesh`, change `flesh-storefront`.

**Learned**:
- `changed_lines` se mide del árbol de inicio del intento al árbol actual, no del commit del slice. Un intento que queda abierto acumula todo lo que pase después y se vuelve incerrable por presupuesto.
- **Regla operativa: settlear cada intento apenas el slice queda verde y committeado.** Dejarlo abierto obliga a un reset autorizado por el maintainer.
- El `--expected-revision` es optimistic locking: cualquier operación previa, incluso una que falla, mueve la revisión.
- Ver [[sdd/flesh-storefront/apply-progress]].

observations.content:

observations.title: El ritmo vertical de la página sale del padding del frame Content, no de los componentes
observations.content:
**What**: Medido directo sobre los artboards de pen.dev (documento `ed824ca8-f10b-4497-a449-9db1727fba69`) el 2026-09-01. El frame `Content` de cada pantalla es `layout: vertical` + `justifyContent: space_between` + `alignItems: center`, y su padding es:

- Landing / Desktop (`P4CKG`): `[44, 0, 40, 0]` — top 44, bottom 40, sin padding horizontal.
- Landing / Mobile (`ByTD6`): `[30, 16, 26, 16]` — top 30, bottom 26, **16 de padding horizontal**.
- PDP / Desktop (`Giwf2`): `[44, 0]` + `gap: 20`.
- PDP / Mobile (`QOzfV`): `[26, 20, 30, 20]` + `gap: 20`.

**Why**: En PR5b el agente aplicó el 44/30 como `py-*` simétrico en el Header, porque el brief decía "vertical padding" sin más. Es incorrecto: ese 44 es el padding TOP de la página, y el 40 es el padding BOTTOM de la misma página — no hay padding vertical propio del header. Corregido a `pt-7.5 md:pt-11` en el Header; el Footer ya estaba bien con `pb-6.5 md:pb-10`. Header y Footer son los dos extremos del mismo padding de página.

**Where**: `src/components/shared/header.tsx`, `src/components/shared/footer.tsx`. Commit `1e95e78`.

**Learned**:
- El `space-between` del frame `Content` es lo que empuja el footer abajo. **El cableado de página (PR6b para landing, PR8a para PDP) es quien debe poner `min-h-screen` + `flex flex-col justify-between`** — ningún componente del shell lo hace por su cuenta.
- **El padding horizontal de 16px en mobile todavía no lo pone nadie.** No está en el Header ni en el Footer porque es padding de página. PR6b tiene que agregarlo o el contenido queda pegado a los bordes en mobile.
- Los tamaños del wordmark en los artboards son consistentes en aspecto (2.51:1): 185×74 desktop, 112×45 mobile. El 218×87 del PDP desktop es deriva del artboard, no requisito — se shipeó un solo tamaño.

observations.title: Cross-machine handoff via sync/workstation-handoff branch
observations.content:
**What**: Created `sync/workstation-handoff`, a transport-only branch off `main` carrying `.handoff/` with an `engram export` JSON (all projects) and a full copy of the pen.dev document directory. Never merged into `main` or the `pr*` chain.

**Why**: Engram lives in a machine-local SQLite DB (`~/.engram/engram.db`) and pen.dev documents live in `~/.pencil/documents/<uuid>/` — neither is tracked by git, so a second workstation cannot reach them. The repo is private, so it is a valid transport channel.

**Where**: branch `sync/workstation-handoff`, `.handoff/README.md` documents restore and re-export steps.

**Learned**: A pen.dev document is a DIRECTORY, not a single file — the `.pen` plus a sibling `images/` folder; copying only the `.pen` loses all bitmaps. Restore is `engram import` (merges, does not replace) plus copying the document dir back under `~/.pencil/documents/`. Also: this repo has no local `user.name` set, so commits from a new worktree fail with "empty ident name"; existing history uses `felipe Saracho <felipe.saracho@itrocksweb.com>`.
